papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and matched to task and data constraints, KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD’s benefits are conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, and availability or synthesis of suitable data; these conditions create predictable failure modes that demand task-aware pipelines, explicit robustness and fairness evaluation, and targeted mitigations.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across modalities, especially NLP. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational structure) and are most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data and training practices. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but outcomes depend on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher quality, and distributional robustness; addressing these requires deliberate pipeline design and evaluation targeted to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multi‑level toolkit for turning large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods include matching softened outputs, supervising intermediate representations or attention, and transferring relational structure; they are frequently combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and student-aware architecture design. Practical success requires careful choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, what data (real, augmented, or synthesized) to use for distillation, and how to mitigate risks such as transferred errors, reduced robustness, or loss of rare behaviors. When KD is treated as an integrated, task‑aware pipeline and combined with complementary compression steps, it routinely produces favorable efficiency–performance trade‑offs across vision and NLP applications, although open problems remain in data‑free distillation, robustness transfer, and principled selection of distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving task performance. When treated as a modular toolkit—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align teacher and student (layer mappings, many-to-many matching), how to obtain or synthesize data (real, generated, or data-free), and how to schedule teachers (ensembles, online, or progressive)—KD consistently enables strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but it has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, teacher errors, distribution shift) that require targeted mitigation strategies. This paper argues KD should be the default core of compression pipelines while outlining pragmatic practices and limits for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Barr
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a configurable, multi-signal component of practical compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD can enable compact models that retain much of a teacher’s utility. Realizing that potential requires combining logits- and representation-level signals, integrating complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), handling limited or private data, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be adopted as the default, pipeline-aware approach to compression while research focuses on principled teacher selection, automated signal scheduling, and robustness-aware distillation.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The toolkit includes soft-output (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, data-side interventions (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols), and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical work shows that well-designed distillation frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance, but success depends on careful teacher–student pairing, signal selection, data strategies, and attention to capacity, robustness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Constraints, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models retain much of the utility of high-capacity systems. KD operates across levels of abstraction (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure) and is routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (quantization, pruning, architecture search) and data strategies (use of original data, augmentation, or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many settings, but success is context-dependent: it depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, or robustness. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, practical variants, and actionable recommendations for applying KD effectively in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Preston
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal set of techniques for compressing large ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller, deployable ‘‘student’’ models. Across vision and language settings, KD extends beyond softened-logit matching to include representation-level alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, staged or progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and data-free workflows, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, whether and how to synthesize or reuse data, and how to evaluate rare-case, robustness, and fairness behaviors determine practical success. While well-designed KD pipelines routinely produce compact models that retain much of teacher utility, predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain shift, propagation of teacher artifacts, and data-privacy constraints—remain active areas for research and engineering.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision, speech, and NLP. KD includes matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, and conveying relational or structural signals; it is often combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The effectiveness of KD depends on deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity and architectural alignment, the distillation data regime (original, augmented, or synthesized), and training schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, or self-distillation). While KD routinely yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs, it has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, propagated teacher errors or biases, and degraded long-tail or out-of-distribution behavior—so reliable deployment treats KD as the starting point of a holistic, task-aware compression pipeline that incorporates complementary techniques and explicit robustness and evaluation practices.

papers_seen.author: Kline
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task‑Aware Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach that should be treated as the default core of model compression workflows in deep learning and NLP. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of original performance when applied with task-aware design. Its strengths arise from diverse transfer mechanisms (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives), hybrid data strategies (original, augmented, synthetic, or data‑free), and composition with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). KD’s effectiveness is conditional on student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and explicit attention to robustness and rare-case behaviors; therefore, practical deployment requires KD-centered, pipeline-based engineering that combines appropriate transfer signals, student pretraining or architecture adaptation, curriculum or staged schedules, and privacy- or data-aware strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. A wide variety of KD strategies—matching softened logits, aligning features or attention maps, multi-teacher schedules, and data- or task-aware augmentation—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on what is distilled, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and provenance of data, and task-specific constraints (e.g., robustness or federated heterogeneity). Carefully designed pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing resource cost, but KD also has important failure modes that motivate complementary techniques and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible, task-aware toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, student pretraining), distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of a teacher’s utility. Realizing those gains in practice requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational structure), how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to source or synthesize distillation data under privacy or data-limited constraints, and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and domain-shift behavior. Responsible deployment therefore treats knowledge distillation as a core element of an integrated compression pipeline, with targeted interventions to mitigate capacity mismatch, teacher error transfer, and data- or distribution-driven failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models from large teachers. When treated as a system-aware procedure—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, using data augmentation or synthesis, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving much of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on careful design: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and domain shift determine real-world success.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep-learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation—regularly yield large runtime, memory, and latency gains when paired with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to prepare distillation data. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on student capacity, data availability, modality alignment, and complementary compression steps. I argue that KD should be treated as a configurable, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a single recipe, and I give practical design principles for when and how to apply it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Barker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of a Composable Compression Toolkit: A Practical Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high-leverage method for producing compact models that retain much of a larger teacher’s performance. KD provides multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational objectives) and is effective across modalities when paired with task-aware data and architecture choices. However, KD by itself is not always sufficient: capacity mismatch, limited or private data, domain shift, and safety-critical behaviors require complementary techniques and careful evaluation. I argue KD should be the default starting point for compression pipelines but must be designed and combined with other methods (pruning, quantization, data strategies, federated protocols) to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Levy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Insufficient Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile engineering toolkit that transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students by matching outputs, features, attention, or relational structure. KD routinely yields large efficiency gains in vision and NLP when tailored to task constraints, student capacity, and available data, but it is not a universal solution: capacity and architecture mismatch, limited or private data, teacher imperfections, and robustness and fairness concerns limit what KD can achieve alone. Reliable compression in production settings therefore treats KD as a core component of a broader pipeline that includes architecture design, complementary compression (pruning, quantization), careful data strategies, and targeted interventions to preserve robustness and rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often retaining much of the original performance. A rich ecosystem of KD variants—logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational/objective transfers, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols—has been developed and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. KD is powerful in practice but has known limits related to teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability or privacy constraints, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and distributional shifts; addressing these requires hybrid pipelines, careful objective design, and attention to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for turning large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD operates by transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational statistics, and can be combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). When used in task-aware pipelines and matched to student capacity and data constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve a substantial fraction of teacher performance; however, its success is conditional on careful teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare-case behaviors, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task‑Aware Engine of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central mechanism in model‑compression workflows for deep learning and NLP: it provides flexible, multi‑signal transfer channels that recover much of a teacher’s utility while enabling latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is conditional — its success depends on explicit choices about which signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, the provenance or synthesis of distillation data, and integration with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Responsible deployment therefore embeds KD in validated, task‑aware pipelines that evaluate robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behavior rather than relying on one‑shot distillation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable deployment of large pretrained models by transferring function or representation from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) ones. Across supervised, self-supervised, and data-free settings, KD methods exploit soft targets, intermediate representation matching, architectural surgery, and data or training-time modifications to improve student accuracy, robustness, or efficiency. Empirical results show that appropriately designed distillation can retain most teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size, precision, or inference cost; but effectiveness depends on choices of targets, data, and teacher-student compatibility. Open challenges include preserving rare-token behavior in distilled NLP models, mitigating bias transfer, and jointly optimizing hardware constraints and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable means to compress large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. When matched to task constraints—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, how to align layers or features, and whether or how to handle missing or private training data—KD enables deployment of competitive models in latency- and resource-constrained settings. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: careful design (task-aware layer selection, many-to-many mapping for large pre-trained transformers, selective sample weighting, and data-free procedures when needed) is required to avoid propagating teacher errors, worsening robustness, or underfitting compact students. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, but that success depends on matching KD mechanisms to application constraints and combining KD with complementary engineering (efficient distillation pipelines and synthetic-data or adversarial generators when data are unavailable).

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression — A Task‑Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible mechanism for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. KD routinely recovers substantial teacher performance when integrated into a broader compression workflow that attends to student capacity, data availability, pretraining, and complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). However, KD has predictable failure modes — capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, degraded long‑tail or robustness behavior, and task‑specific limits — that require explicit mitigation and evaluation. A design‑sensitive pipeline that treats KD as the default first step but pairs it with pretraining, targeted distillation signals, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives yields the most reliable route to compact, deployable models across vision and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD spans simple logit-based supervision to richer representation-, relation-, and adversarial-level transfers and is used to enable on-device inference, multi-task models, domain specialization, privacy-aware releases, and data-limited deployments. Best outcomes arise when KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), task-aware design, careful sample or synthetic-data strategies, and interventions for bias and privacy. KD has clear empirical benefits across modalities but also well-documented limits—sensitivity to data availability and heterogeneity, potential propagation of teacher errors or biases, and the need for architectural and optimization care—motivating principled adaptations and further study.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, flexible strategy for compressing and adapting deep models for real-world deployment. When framed as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, teacher ensembles, data-aware synthesis, and architecture-aware compression—KD routinely yields compact students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to address robustness and rare-event behavior; when these are handled explicitly, KD enables reliable, deployable models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Banks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multimodal family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models retain much of teacher utility while meeting deployment constraints. KD now encompasses softened-output matching, intermediate-representation and attention matching, relational objectives, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies including augmentation and synthesis. Its strengths make KD the natural default starting point for compression, but reliable deployment requires integrating KD into a task-aware pipeline that addresses capacity alignment, data provenance, complementary compression primitives, and robustness and fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Stokes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a multifaceted and practical paradigm for producing compact, deployable neural models from larger teachers. Modern distillation transfers information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure—and is commonly integrated with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical distillation workflows emphasize task- and data-aware choices (which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to prepare or synthesize distillation data) and often use multi-stage or progressive schedules. Empirical work shows distilled students frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance across NLP and other modalities, but success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data regime and distribution match. Key limitations and open problems include optimization and capacity mismatch, robustness and fairness transfer, domain-shift behavior, and principled methods for operating without original training data. Best practices center on making KD a configurable component of a broader, hybrid compression pipeline rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Fitzpatrick
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical toolkit for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. A range of distillation signals—soft targets, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, and ensemble or online schedules—can be selected and combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity and data conditions; however, predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, distribution shift, and degraded long-tail behavior) require task-aware pipelines, careful data strategies, and explicit robustness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, modality-agnostic approach to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as the default starting point for compression, KD provides multiple complementary signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) that—when matched to student capacity and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—produce strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is not universally sufficient: practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability and provenance, domain shift, teacher errors, and robustness/fairness constraints. A pragmatic compression pipeline therefore places KD at its center but integrates pretraining, architecture adaptation, data-aware distillation schedules, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational structure, and often combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled models can recover much of teacher performance on vision and language tasks, but success depends on what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, data availability and selection, and training protocols. Practical deployment requires addressing optimization challenges, teacher imperfection, domain shift, and distributional issues such as low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System: Practical Strengths, Limits, and Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system—combining soft-target supervision, representation-level objectives, data augmentation, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—KD reliably yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. Effectiveness depends on handling data availability, architecture mismatches, and undesirable teacher artifacts; these constraints are manageable when KD is designed with domain adaptation, input alignment, and augmentation-aware strategies. I argue KD should be the default toolchain for producing production-ready compact models, applied with explicit attention to what knowledge is transferred and how it is matched to student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure, and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization) and with data- or curriculum-driven strategies. Across vision, language, generative models, and policy settings, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory; however, it has clear limits related to capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data availability, and optimization instability. Real-world deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable engineering toolkit rather than a single recipe, combining careful choice of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while attempting to retain performance. Across computer vision and natural language processing, KD variants address constraints such as limited computation, on-device heterogeneity, lack of access to teacher training data, fairness concerns, and the need for task-specific efficiency. Common themes include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate representations, using multiple teachers or self-generated targets, and integrating compression with architecture search or pre-training. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact, practical models for deployment, but also reveals optimization and data-dependence limitations that motivate method refinements like task-adaptive search, multi-teacher weighting, data-free synthesis, and self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical, multifaceted toolkit for converting large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. The toolkit includes transferring softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based transfers, online and multi-teacher protocols, and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation objectives, data sources, and teacher–student design are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy, optimization stability, domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors in language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Grimes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models so as to meet constraints on latency, memory, or privacy. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-target matching to include intermediate representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and synthetic-data approaches). In practice, KD is most effective when integrated into a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that may include pretraining of compact architectures, pruning, quantization, and architecture search; success depends on aligning distilled signals with student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and explicitly evaluating robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors. Open problems remain in principled teacher selection and weighting, reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and edge-case behavior, and ensuring robustness under distribution shift and adversarial conditions.

papers_seen.author: Pollard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller, faster students and has become a practical foundation for model compression across vision and NLP. KD methods span softened-output matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-centric strategies including augmentation and synthesis. While KD often yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss, its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data, robustness, and privacy constraints. Combined pipelines that integrate KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design deliver the best deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become central for deploying high-performing deep models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has developed a spectrum of techniques — from soft-target supervision and intermediate-layer transfer to multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants — and combined distillation with pruning and architecture search to compress large transformers and other architectures. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains (speed, memory, privacy) and fundamental tradeoffs (bias–variance, data heterogeneity, and information loss), pointing to hybrid protocols and adaptive selection of distillation signals as promising directions.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The field includes matching softened output distributions, imitating intermediate representations or attention maps, transferring relational or structural knowledge, and combining distillation with data-side techniques (augmentation, synthetic data) and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing parameters and latency, but effectiveness depends on choices of knowledge to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, fairness and bias transfer, privacy in distributed settings, and limits to compression for some generative tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practicalities, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted approach for transferring learned behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques operate at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level replacements) and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). Practical success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and provenance, and careful alignment of objectives; unresolved issues include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, handling rare-token or tail behaviors in NLP, domain shift and robustness, and principled distillation without access to original data.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a versatile, production-ready set of techniques for shrinking large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students that often retain most of the teachers' utility. Its practical value is highest when KD is treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization). However, KD’s success is conditional on data availability, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, and careful evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Regularizing, and Flexible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Beyond simple logit matching, KD encompasses transferring intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behavior; it can be applied with or without access to original training data and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. KD often acts as an implicit regularizer that shapes the learning dynamics of students, and careful design of what to transfer and how—along with adaptations for data scarcity, privacy, and distributed settings—determines practical success. While KD is not a universal solution and depends on choices about teacher design, data, and alignment strategies, a hybrid, task-aware KD protocol enables high-quality compression across modalities and deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure). Over the past decade KD evolved from simple logit matching to a flexible, task-aware toolkit that interoperates with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies (including data-free and federated variants). Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity and available data, and on careful evaluation for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, preserving out-of-distribution and rare-case performance, and reliable distillation under privacy or data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modular approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a configurable pipeline—choosing what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supply or synthesize distillation data—KD routinely yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: student capacity, data provenance or availability, teacher quality, and robustness/fairness concerns limit naïve application. Responsible deployment therefore requires combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), careful teacher–student alignment, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, low-frequency token degradation, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened outputs to a multi-signal toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware strategies (including data-free synthesis). In practice KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design), and when distillation choices are matched to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. However, predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, optimization instability, and degraded long-tail or out-of-distribution behavior—require explicit mitigations, careful evaluation, and continued methodological work to preserve robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal representations. A rich set of mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, feature or representation imitation, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers, and data-free or privacy-aware strategies—has been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher accuracy while substantially reducing latency and footprint, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, data and augmentation strategies, teacher quality, and training schedules. Ongoing work focuses on robustness to domain shift, heterogeneous devices, limited or unavailable data, and principled ways to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescriptive Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a central toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware or data-free strategies, and integration with other compression primitives—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, or preservation of rare behaviors; realizing reliable compressed models requires deliberate teacher preparation, student-aware design, data or synthesis strategies, and explicit robustness and bias interventions.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core—and Bounded—Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search)—KD routinely enables deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and evaluation of robustness and fairness; thus KD should be treated as a central element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core, practical approach for converting large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks KD operates as a toolkit—transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, and using relational or teacher-ensemble signals—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Success depends on student capacity, the complexity and provenance of distillation data, and careful teacher–student alignment; when these are addressed, distilled students can recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include preserving rare-token behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and principled methods for teacher selection and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD succeeds when its design (what to transfer, how to map representations, and how to prepare data and teachers) is matched to the student capacity, task structure, and deployment constraints. While KD is not a panacea, when combined with complementary compression techniques and data-aware procedures it enables efficient, robust models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Hester
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multi-signal toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, and how to manage data (real, augmented, or synthetic). Common challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, degraded robustness under domain shift, and limited-data or privacy-constrained settings; these motivate complementary techniques such as multi-stage distillation, teacher curricula, student pretraining, data-free synthesis, and targeted evaluation for safety and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Murray

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring learned behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under latency, memory, or device heterogeneity constraints. KD spans multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), training schedules (multi-stage, multi-teacher, online), and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic). While KD routinely yields strong empirical gains, its reliability depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teachers and students, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; thus KD should be treated as a central component of compression pipelines but combined with complementary methods and careful validation for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Reynolds
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses functionality from larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. A diverse set of KD variants — softened-logit matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data‑free or privacy-aware protocols — has enabled substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when training pipelines address teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints. Persistent challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors (important in NLP), robustness and fairness under distillation, and producing reliable distilled models when original training data are limited or private.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention patterns—and often yields substantial improvements in latency, memory, and deployability relative to naive student training. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and privacy constraints, and whether complementary compression methods are applied. Viewed as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables flexible, task-aware compression pipelines that can be adapted to real-world constraints while acknowledging remaining limits around robustness, data-free operation, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central Tool, Insufficient Alone — An Integrated Workflow for Reliable Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical mechanism for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robust, fair, and deployable students: its effectiveness depends on student capacity and architecture, teacher quality, the provenance and coverage of distillation data, and complementary compression primitives. A reliable compression strategy treats KD as the central gearbox within a broader, task-aware pipeline that includes student-friendly architecture design or pretraining, careful signal selection (logits, features, attention, relational constraints), curating or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and combining KD with pruning/quantization and rigorous robustness and privacy evaluations.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system — combining softened-output matching, intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary compression primitives such as pruning or quantization — KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, addressing data-availability constraints, and mitigating risks from imperfect teachers, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift. I argue KD should be the default component of production compression pipelines provided practitioners adopt task-aware recipes, incorporate data-aware and architecture-aware remedies, and monitor robustness and fairness outcomes.
