papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression methods form a versatile toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Work in the past decade has expanded simple teacher→student logit matching into a broad set of techniques that match intermediate representations, exploit attention or structural signals, operate with or without access to original training data, and combine with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search). Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher quality across language, vision, and retrieval tasks when distillation objectives, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen deliberately. Important practical concerns remain: optimization and capacity mismatches that limit perfect teacher replication, distributional or privacy constraints on distillation data, and trade-offs between fidelity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger, higher-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Across NLP and broader deep-learning tasks, a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Distillation is both a practical engineering toolkit for deployment constraints (latency, memory, heterogeneity, privacy) and an active research area that raises challenges around preserving robustness, handling domain and data shifts, and designing principled curricula and teacher signals for maximal downstream utility.

papers_seen.author: Hines
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted toolkit for producing compact models from large teachers. KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational structure), and is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary operations such as pruning and quantization. Distillation routinely yields favorable efficiency–performance trade-offs, but its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, alignment between teacher and student, and availability or synthesis of suitable data; remaining challenges include propagation of teacher errors, robustness under distributional shift, privacy-aware protocols, and principled automated design for diverse deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/structural signals) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and suitable data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols). While KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across modalities, its success depends on student capacity, availability and provenance of data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization choices; these constraints motivate hybrid pipelines and application-aware evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Bishop
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, multi-signal approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When embedded in an explicit compression pipeline and matched to student capacity and data availability, KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance. However, its reliability is conditional: capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, limited or mismatched data, and distributional shift produce predictable failure modes that require complementary methods and task-aware remedies. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a central but conditional engine of compression, combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and targeted evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) functions as a flexible, engineering-first mechanism for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a multifaceted toolbox rather than a single trick, KD enables compact models through combinations of soft-target matching, representation-level supervision, multi-teacher or staged schedules, and data-side strategies. However, KD is not a guaranteed solution by itself: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, optimization dynamics, and attention to robustness and bias; therefore reliable deployment requires integrating KD into hybrid pipelines that include student pre-training, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression steps such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Griffin
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Research and engineering practice have established a toolkit of distillation signals (soft output or logit transfer, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational objectives), schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher), and data strategies (real-data, augmented, synthetic, or data-free). KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities, but important failure modes remain—capacity mismatch, propagated teacher errors (especially on rare tokens or long-tail behavior), domain shift, limited-data regimes, and privacy concerns—motivating hybrid pipelines, task-aware signal selection, and continued research on principled, robust, and privacy-preserving distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD encompasses transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure; it can be combined with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, parameter sharing) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic generation, data‑free rehearsal) to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey remedy: optimization challenges, teacher–student mismatches, data or domain shift, and risk of propagating teacher errors require task‑aware design, complementary compression methods, and careful validation. When applied as a principled toolkit — choosing what to transfer, how to align representations, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to integrate pruning/quantization — KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Toward Integrated Feature-, Data- and Robustness-aware Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from simple logit matching into a toolbox of complementary techniques. Empirical and theoretical work shows that (1) matching internal features often transfers richer representations than logits alone, (2) the choice of input-side interventions (e.g., data augmentation) substantially changes distillation dynamics, and (3) robustness, teacher quality, and sample selection must be addressed explicitly. I argue that effective model compression in deep learning and NLP requires integrating feature-level mimicry with careful input-space design, selective or confidence-weighted teacher signals, and robustness-aware objectives. This combined approach maximizes student performance while keeping models compact and deployment-ready.

papers_seen.author: Barr
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a configurable, multi-signal component of practical compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD can enable compact models that retain much of a teacher’s utility. Realizing that potential requires combining logits- and representation-level signals, integrating complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), handling limited or private data, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be adopted as the default, pipeline-aware approach to compression while research focuses on principled teacher selection, automated signal scheduling, and robustness-aware distillation.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Pre-training Plus Strategic Distillation: Practical Principles for Compressing Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when combined with deliberate choices about pre-training, the form of knowledge transferred, data manipulation during distillation, and adaptive teacher-student dynamics. Compact models that are pre-trained, trained to mimic both outputs and internal representations, and exposed to carefully designed augmented or mixed inputs can match much of the performance of larger models while meeting deployment constraints. However, compression success depends critically on optimization, data distribution, and task-specific phenomena such as rare-word behavior in sequence generation. I argue that a pragmatic pipeline—pre-train compact architectures, distill soft targets and internal representations, use augmentation/mixing to shape training data complexity, and apply adaptive or meta-learned teacher strategies—offers the best trade-off between efficiency and accuracy for deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, multi-signal toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance when its signals, data, and teacher–student design are carefully chosen and when it is integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). At the same time, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: student capacity, data availability or provenance, teacher quality, and robustness/fairness concerns all shape outcomes. This synthesis summarizes what is known about KD’s methods, mechanisms, practical benefits, and remaining challenges, and outlines recommended pipeline principles for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Armstrong
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically driven set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can be combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free protocols). Empirical results across vision and language show KD often recovers most teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness, long-tail behavior, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques compress large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches range from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and using contrastive or projection-based objectives. Practical training choices—such as which layers or features to mimic, how to filter or weight training samples, the role of data augmentation, and whether compact models are pre-trained—strongly affect outcomes. KD has been applied across domains (vision, language, graphs), combined with quantization and low-precision deployment, and adapted for resource-heterogeneous and latency-sensitive settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights that KD works both by transferring relational/representational knowledge and by providing regularizing soft targets; effective distillation designs balance these mechanisms and tailor the transfer to task and capacity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a composable engineering toolkit rather than a single loss or recipe. Effective compression combines representation-level transfer, student pretraining, data-side interventions (real, augmented, or synthetic), progressive or self-distillation schedules, and explicit robustness- and privacy-aware objectives. When these components are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints, distilled models can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements; careless application, by contrast, risks capacity mismatch and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural networks so they can run efficiently in production and on resource-constrained devices. Recent work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, and that a range of complementary techniques—data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, internal representation matching, layer alignment, meta-learning of teachers, and robustness-aware objectives—meaningfully improve student quality or transfer desirable properties. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on optimization, the choice of teacher/student architectures, and the distributional complexity of the training data. I argue that best practice for KD in deep learning and NLP is to treat it as a family of methods to be combined—augmenting data, distilling intermediate representations, leveraging multiple or adaptive teachers, and explicitly distilling robustness—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, system‑level approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD combines multiple transfer signals and data strategies and is most effective when embedded in an integrated compression workflow that accounts for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical recipes pair KD with pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data synthesis or augmentation to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. Remaining challenges include capacity and optimization gaps between teachers and students, propagation of teacher errors or biases, reliable distillation without original training data, and robustness under domain shift; addressing these requires task‑aware choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to prepare or synthesize distillation data.

papers_seen.author: Hester
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multi-signal toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, and how to manage data (real, augmented, or synthetic). Common challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, degraded robustness under domain shift, and limited-data or privacy-constrained settings; these motivate complementary techniques such as multi-stage distillation, teacher curricula, student pretraining, data-free synthesis, and targeted evaluation for safety and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Empirical work across vision and language shows KD can preserve most of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy demands. Practical KD spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, multi-teacher and staged schedules, student-aware teacher adaptation, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and integrating KD into broader compression and evaluation pipelines to address robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the System-Level Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and flexible paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students for deep learning and NLP. Treated as a system-level toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD supports multiple transfer objectives (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), composes with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), and enables deployment in data- or privacy-constrained scenarios. However, realizing those benefits in production requires careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and robustness degradation under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and empirically effective family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and deployment constraints, KD enables moving from research-stage, high-capacity architectures to resource-efficient models suitable for latency- and privacy-constrained production. Realizing KD's full potential requires attention to teacher quality, data and domain mismatches, and scalability; appropriate choices—representation-level objectives, multi-teacher signals, online protocols, and privacy-aware distillation—address these challenges and make KD a core tool for applied deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, modular technique in modern model-compression pipelines: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller students while remaining flexible enough to combine with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-side interventions. KD’s practical success depends on deliberate choices—what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to evaluate robustness and long-tail behavior. When used as part of a system that addresses optimization, data, and mismatch issues, KD frequently yields compact models that meet deployment constraints; when used alone or carelessly it can underperform or propagate undesirable behaviors. The remainder of this paper argues for KD as the default, central component of compression toolkits while outlining its limits and concrete design recommendations to mitigate them.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a principal, practical approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers across vision, speech, and NLP tasks. A rich family of distillation signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational structure), schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher), and data protocols (real-data, augmented, synthesized, and data-free) has been developed. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when teacher–student design, data provenance, and deployment constraints are considered explicitly. However, KD has well-documented limits — notably teacher–student capacity mismatch, sensitivity to data availability and domain shift, and the risk of transferring teacher errors or undesirable behaviors — which motivate integrated, task-aware compression pipelines and targeted mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Singleton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a teacher to a student through soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and ensemble signals. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when its design is adapted to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but open challenges remain in preserving robustness, rare-token behavior, handling data- or privacy-constrained settings, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relationships. Methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate features or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when originals are unavailable, and designing architecture-aware layer mappings. KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and used across modalities (vision, language, generative models) to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and propagation of biases.

While KD routinely yields deployable models that recover much of teacher performance, its effectiveness is conditional on capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for transferring information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. KD techniques span output-level supervision (soft logits), intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, self- and progressive distillation, and data-free or zero-shot variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (vision, speech, translation, detection, and generation) while enabling on-device and real-time use; success depends on the choice of distillation targets, the match between teacher and student capacity, the availability and quality of data, and appropriate regularization or augmentation during training. Practical deployment typically combines KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and privacy-aware mechanisms to produce robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Luna
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring behavioral and representational information to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). A versatile set of distillation signals and protocols—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational objectives, multi- and self-teaching, and data-side techniques including synthetic or data-free approaches—has been developed and routinely combined with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware student design). KD often produces sizable efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment needs, but practical use requires attention to capacity mismatch, teacher errors and biases, domain shift, and preservation of rare/long-tail behaviors. Best practice treats KD as the central component of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe.

When combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, KD often yields students that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, data availability, robustness, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. In practice KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data-management strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD routinely enables large reductions in parameters and inference cost with modest drops in accuracy, challenges remain in handling domain shift, limited or private data, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors and biases.

papers_seen.author: White

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques to transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. papers_seen.author: Torres

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD works at multiple levels — soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behaviour — and is most effective when combined with data strategies, teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression such as pruning or quantization. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can regularize student training, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align capacities, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; careful, task-aware protocols are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD methods transfer information through softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational objectives, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and varied data strategies (real, augmented, synthetic, or data-free). Empirical evidence shows KD often attains favorable efficiency–performance trade-offs when distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and data protocols are chosen to match task and deployment constraints. However, limits remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and robustness under distribution shift; addressing these requires hybrid pipelines, representation-aware objectives, and careful evaluation for fairness and reliability.

papers_seen.author: Bautista
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, multi-level set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when treated as a central element of a broader compression pipeline—paired with careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation data or augmentation, and complementary methods such as quantization, pruning, or architecture search. However, KD is not a universal cure: capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, domain or data mismatch, and optimization instability create predictable failure modes that demand conditional design choices and careful evaluation. Practitioners should therefore adopt KD as a default tool, applied thoughtfully and combined with other techniques to produce robust, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. Research spans theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps, practical methods for compressing pretrained language models, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, strategies to preserve robustness, and distributed/federated adaptations. Methods include soft-label matching, intermediate feature/attention imitation, many-to-many layer mappings, task-adaptive architecture search, and self-distillation. Empirical and theoretical work highlights gains in efficiency and deployment feasibility across vision and NLP tasks, while also revealing limitations related to data distribution, teacher quality, robustness, and low-frequency token coverage. Open directions include principled handling of imperfect teachers, domain adaptation during compression, robustness-aware distillation, and scalable distillation in distributed or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Ewing
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal, pipeline-oriented approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, progressive or module-replacement schedules, and multi- or self-distillation schemes. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with deliberate data strategies (original-data augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols). Its empirical strengths are conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, alignment of signals to architecture, and robust evaluation for distribution shift, fairness, and privacy. Emerging work addresses data-free distillation and progressive module-replacing strategies, while open problems remain around principled objective selection, preserving rare-case behavior, and automation of architecture-agnostic pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across computer vision, speech, multimodal, and NLP tasks, distillation protocols—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature and attention-based transfers—enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Success depends on careful choices of distillation targets, teacher-student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, low-precision, architecture search, or federated protocols) it yields deployable models for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Gordon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. When KD is treated as the core of a compression pipeline and matched to deployment constraints, it routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs. However, KD is design-sensitive: its reliability depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives. Responsible deployment therefore requires KD-centered pipelines that address capacity mismatch, data limitations, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal training paradigm for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Empirically, KD preserves much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks when its objectives, data, and student architecture are chosen to match deployment constraints. Reliable compression in production requires KD to be integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with task-aware choices to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, teacher-induced errors, and degraded long-tail or fairness-sensitive behavior.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Practical Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core set of techniques for converting large, expensive neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for real-world deployment. KD variants transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural behaviors; they can be combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture modification) and adapted for constrained data, privacy, and deployment regimes. However, distillation’s success depends on principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate teacher-induced errors or biases. Practical deployments therefore require task-aware distillation design, careful teacher selection or adaptation, and evaluation of failure modes such as degraded rare-token behavior or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Goodman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Pipeline-Oriented Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When used as a configurable, multi-stage pipeline that combines multiple distillation signals, student pretraining, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, sensitivity to distribution shift, and data or privacy limits—that require targeted remedies and careful evaluation. Treated as the central element of a composable compression workflow rather than a single recipe, KD enables practical, responsible model deployment across deep learning and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single training trick into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for shrinking large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD methods transfer teacher signals at different levels — final soft outputs, intermediate features, relational or attention structure — and are often combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, choosing what and how to transfer, handling data availability (including data-free scenarios), and addressing robustness and privacy constraints. When KD is designed with these considerations it can substantially reduce inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, though open problems remain around domain shift, rare-token behaviors, and reliably transferring robustness.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broadly useful, multi-signal approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal representations at multiple levels and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques, careful data strategies, and architecture-aware design. Practical success typically requires matching distillation objectives to student capacity, handling limited or private data (including synthetic or data-free regimes), and explicitly evaluating robustness, rare-event behavior, and fairness. Despite substantial empirical gains, open challenges remain in principled objective design, reliable transfer under domain shift or privacy constraints, and preserving calibration and rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Swanson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for producing compact models from large teachers to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), it routinely yields deployable students that recover much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, and targeted evaluation of robustness and long‑tail behaviors; therefore KD should be treated as the default first step in compression pipelines but embedded in hybrid, task‑aware workflows that explicitly address known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Spence
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. The approach spans matching teacher outputs, imitating intermediate representations, distilling relational structure, and combining distillation with architecture- and data-side interventions. KD is widely used to reduce inference cost and memory footprint, enable on-device and privacy-aware deployment, and adapt models across domains; its success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and mitigation of bias and robustness trade-offs. Practical pipelines treat KD as a central, composable element combined with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and task-aware data strategies to produce compact models that approach teacher performance under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lester
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a multifaceted, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Contemporary KD expands beyond softened-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, layer alignment and projector mappings, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware protocols (including data-free or synthetic-data approaches). When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with task- and capacity-aware teacher–student design, KD routinely yields small models that retain much of teacher utility. Remaining challenges center on capacity and optimization mismatch, distributional shift and robustness, propagation of teacher errors and bias, and distillation under data- or privacy-constrained settings. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a composable process that must be designed around the deployment task and evaluated beyond aggregate accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default but Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, multi-signal method for converting large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. As a modular component it can transfer logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals, or ensembles; be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation; and operate in constrained settings including federated, privacy-sensitive, or data-scarce regimes. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy/efficiency trade-offs when student capacity, data strategy, and signal alignment are chosen deliberately, but it has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors or biases, sensitivity to domain shift, and limits under scarce or private data—that require integration with complementary methods and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Grant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while aiming to preserve task performance. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a diverse set of techniques that supervise logits, internal representations, attention maps, and relational structures, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data strategies. Despite widespread practical success across vision and language tasks, KD’s effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability and provenance, and training dynamics; open problems include reliably preserving rare behaviors, automating signal selection, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and flexible mechanism for producing compact, deployable models across modalities. Treated as the central element of a compression pipeline, KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teachers into smaller students, and when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data strategies it routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest loss in task performance. However, KD alone is insufficient in many production settings: capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, data availability (including data-free methods), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior must all be addressed to produce reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Butler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Composable Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for producing compact neural models from larger teachers. KD supplies multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational patterns) and, when combined with complementary compression primitives and careful data and architecture choices, enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD alone does not eliminate capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, data scarcity, or robustness and fairness risks; reliable compression therefore treats KD as the central component of a broader, task‑aware pipeline that includes explicit evaluation and mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible suite of techniques for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression workflow but adapted to task, architecture, and data constraints, KD routinely yields substantial improvements in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Its utility spans logits-based supervision, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free pipelines. KD is not a turnkey solution: reliable deployment requires complementary methods (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful handling of teacher imperfections and limited or private data, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a mere optimization trick but a central, versatile toolkit for compressing large models into compact, deployable students. When treated as a system composed of complementary ingredients—teacher design (single, ensemble or multi-teacher), what to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, relational information), how to obtain data (real, synthesized, or data-free), and deployment constraints (privacy, federated or on-device latency)—KD consistently enables strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance across vision, language, generative, and real-world production tasks. Realizing KD’s full potential requires representation- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive teacher–student mappings, careful handling of data scarcity or privacy, and integration with pretraining and other compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective mechanism for producing compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of the original performance. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and adapted to task needs—by choosing appropriate distillation signals, pretraining students, leveraging multi-teacher or staged schedules, and addressing data or rare-token issues—KD yields reliable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, its benefits are conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data alignment, and safeguards against propagated errors; therefore KD should be the default starting point for compression, used together with complementary techniques and evaluation practices to ensure robustness in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Singleton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach that can enable deployment of high-performing deep models by producing smaller, faster students. Its strengths arise from transferring softened outputs and richer representational signals, and from composability with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: reliable deployment requires task-aware design, careful handling of data and capacity mismatch, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-case behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Fischer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD combines soft-target matching, representation- and relation-level supervision, multi-teacher schedules, and data-side strategies to produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, and attention to robustness and bias; consequently, reliable deployment treats KD as a core component of hybrid compression pipelines that also use pretraining, architecture-aware design, pruning, and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Whitney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD has evolved beyond simple softened-logit matching into a family of methods that transfer intermediate representations, relational structure, or curriculum/sampling strategies, and that operate in online, multi-teacher, or data-limited regimes. Practical success depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives to address robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher (or ensemble) models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) while retaining most of the teacher’s utility. Across vision, speech, generative modeling, and NLP, practitioners use multiple KD signals (soft targets, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes) and combine KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware student design). Empirical practice and synthesis work show KD yields substantial efficiency gains when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data availability, and task constraints; remaining challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, reliable distillation without original data, and preserving robustness, fairness, and rare or low-frequency behaviors under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable framework for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. As a first-line technique it reliably recovers much of teacher performance while enabling latency, memory, and privacy constrained deployments; however, KD alone is insufficient for many real-world requirements. Effective compression treats KD as the core of a broader, task-aware pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, complementary compression primitives, data strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides a rich set of transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and composes naturally with architecture search, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success is conditional on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher quality, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be treated as the default, configurable first-line technique in compression pipelines, but only when combined with task-aware choices and complementary methods that mitigate its predictable failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so the latter can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The toolkit includes matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate representations and attention, relational or contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, and data-aware protocols (including synthetic or data-free inputs). KD is most effective when treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes student pretraining, architecture-aware design, pruning or quantization, and careful selection or synthesis of distillation data. Practical deployment must attend to predictable failure modes — capacity mismatch, data or domain shift, teacher artifacts, and long-tail behavior loss — which motivates hybrid, task-aware distillation strategies and continued research on robustness, fairness, and privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. The literature frames KD as a multi-level toolkit—ranging from soft-target (logit) transfer to intermediate-feature and relational objectives—that is most effective when combined with task-aware data strategies and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data or domain mismatch, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness trade-offs.
