papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Practically, distillation is a multi-signal toolkit—matching soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, and aligning relational or layer-wise structure—and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). Success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, and task constraints; careful engineering choices and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-behavior retention are essential for production-ready deployment.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single training heuristic into a flexible set of methods that enable compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring outputs, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students, distillation can materially reduce model size and inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Practical deployment requires matching the distillation strategy to task and deployment constraints, combining distillation with complementary compression techniques, and addressing limits such as capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and possible propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation targets, preparing the student (often via pre-training), and addressing data, privacy, and robustness constraints—KD yields compact models that retain a substantial fraction of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks. However, its success depends on design choices (what to distill and when), data availability, and mitigation of teacher errors; thus KD is best treated as a system of complementary techniques rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical toolkit to transfer performance and representational structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under memory, compute, or latency constraints. Research has expanded KD beyond simple soft-label matching to encompass intermediate-feature imitation, many-to-many layer mapping, relational and task-aware transfers, multi-teacher fusion, and input-side interventions (e.g., data augmentation or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows distilled students frequently approach teacher performance when methods are matched to the task and architecture, but significant open problems remain around robustness, low-frequency behavior, teacher errors, and data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. Across computer vision, language, generative, and combinatorial domains, KD variants—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and relation-level imitation, layer-wise and progressive schemes, multi-teacher fusion, and data-aware or data-free protocols—enable large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Practical application typically combines KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and depends critically on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and layers, and how to curate or synthesize distillation data. Important limits remain: optimization gaps from capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases (especially for low-frequency phenomena), domain-shift fragility, and privacy or data-availability constraints. Task-aware design, multi-signal objectives, and targeted interventions for robustness and fairness are central to effective, responsible deployment.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable core of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, and the provenance or scarcity of distillation data. Responsible deployment therefore requires task-aware selection of distillation targets, mitigation of propagated teacher errors, and explicit evaluation for robustness and rare-token behaviors.

Its success, however, depends on decisions about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, access to data or synthetic surrogates, and mitigation of robustness and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Treat Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Compression — but Build a Task‑Aware Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high‑value approach for turning large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure using multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) and often composes with pruning, quantization, or architecture changes. However, KD alone cannot guarantee preservation of rare behaviors, robustness under domain shift, or elimination of teacher biases; practical compression succeeds when distillation is the default first step within a carefully designed, task‑aware pipeline that includes projector design, data strategies, capacity alignment, and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practicalities, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted approach for transferring learned behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques operate at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level replacements) and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). Practical success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and provenance, and careful alignment of objectives; unresolved issues include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, handling rare-token or tail behaviors in NLP, domain shift and robustness, and principled distillation without access to original data.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, multi-signal approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the first-line method within a task- and deployment-aware compression pipeline, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP. Its practical success depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize appropriate distillation data, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression primitives and targeted evaluation of robustness and fairness. KD is a powerful backbone for compression but is not sufficient by itself; production-ready systems use KD as the central element of an integrated workflow that addresses capacity mismatch, data constraints, and predictable failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep-learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation—regularly yield large runtime, memory, and latency gains when paired with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to prepare distillation data. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on student capacity, data availability, modality alignment, and complementary compression steps. I argue that KD should be treated as a configurable, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a single recipe, and I give practical design principles for when and how to apply it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, system-level approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to compact students. The KD toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free protocols. In practice KD is often combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture surgery) and student pretraining or domain adaptation to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on task-aware design choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to supply distillation data, and how to monitor transferred errors or biases—and remains conditioned by data availability, teacher quality, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: a Position and Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model compression for deep learning and NLP: it is the most flexible, task-aware mechanism for transferring a teacher’s predictive behavior and internal structure into a deployable student. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), appropriate signal selection (logits, features, relations), and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free samples). However, KD is not a universal panacea — its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and careful handling of robustness and fairness concerns. Thus, engineering KD as a configurable, multi-stage pipeline that integrates representation-level objectives, data-aware protocols, and complementary compression primitives offers the best route to reliable, real-world model compression.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, often ensemble or over-parameterized teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, graph, generative, and language tasks, distillation reduces storage and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher's accuracy. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable. Distillation has been applied successfully to compress transformers and other large pretrained language models, to speed up question answering and reading-comprehension systems, and to produce compact models suitable for deployment on edge devices. At the same time, distillation faces challenges including loss of certain types of teacher knowledge, sensitivity to which samples are distilled, potential transfer or amplification of undesirable biases, and concerns about robustness and privacy. Recent work addresses these issues by selective sample weighting, multi-teacher schemes, adversarial data-free approaches, and robustness-aware objectives, suggesting a rich design space for future improvement.

papers_seen.author: Myers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi‑signal toolkit for converting large teacher models into compact, deployable students. When treated as a design‑sensitive, task‑aware pipeline and combined with complementary compression primitives and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade‑offs for vision and language tasks. Its effectiveness, however, is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, and the availability and provenance of distillation data; therefore reliable deployment requires explicit choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. This article argues that KD should be the default backbone of compression workflows, paired with targeted remedies for its principal failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural networks into compact, deployable models across computer vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD techniques extend beyond matching teacher output probabilities to include distillation of intermediate representations, layer-level mappings, and training without access to original data. Practical applications span compressing generative adversarial networks, pre-trained language models, and low-precision networks, while also addressing robustness and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation protocols can retain most of a teacher's performance or even improve downstream robustness and inference efficiency, though success depends on choices such as what knowledge to transfer, architectural alignment, and availability of data or suitable synthetic surrogates.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central — but Conditional — Paradigm for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. Treated as a configurable pipeline that selects what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to source distillation data, KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. Its strengths are maximized when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful engineering; its limits appear when student capacity, data provenance, or teacher errors and biases are not explicitly handled. This paper argues KD should be the default starting point for compression while emphasizing principled design choices and safeguards to ensure robust, fair, and data-efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. It functions as a multi-signal toolbox—softened output matching, intermediate representation alignment, relational or attention-level transfer, and data-side strategies—that is often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Distillation routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs in vision and language tasks, but its success is conditional on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and provenance, and mitigation of teacher error or bias. Practical deployments therefore treat distillation as one component of an integrated compression pipeline, using task-aware objective design, data strategies (including privacy-preserving or synthesized surrogates), and careful evaluation on rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-driven family of techniques for converting large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for constrained inference. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels—from softened output distributions to intermediate representations, attention and relational patterns—and are routinely combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and 3D tasks shows that well-designed distillation pipelines can retain most teacher utility while substantially reducing parameter count and inference cost; however, practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of robustness, long-tail behaviors, and potential bias propagation.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. KD delivers substantial efficiency gains while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but it is not a single recipe: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, how distillation data are chosen or synthesized, and how complementary compression techniques are applied. Treating KD as a configurable system—combining appropriate loss forms, layer mappings, data strategies, and robustness/privacy safeguards—yields the best trade-offs between compactness and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for compressing large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. Empirical practice treats KD as a configurable pipeline: choosing which teacher signals to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational structure), aligning teacher and student architectures and capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. KD reliably reduces memory and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities, but predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, propagation of teacher errors and biases, domain shift, and degraded long-tail behavior—require careful design choices, complementary methods, and targeted evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, Benefits, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relations. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, distillation variants and complementary compression methods enable substantial reductions in size and latency while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are widely used to transfer behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under resource constraints. Research over the past decade has developed variants that target outputs (soft labels), internal representations (layer-wise and attention-based methods), data regimes (data-free or distilled training sets), and architecture search for task-aware compression. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the practical gains and fundamental limits of distillation, and points to best practices such as pre-training compact models, selecting or synthesizing appropriate training data, and aligning student capacity to distilled signal.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a core component of compression pipelines, KD can transfer information via softened logits, intermediate representations, relational signals, or synthesized data, and it is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data strategies. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the provenance and quantity of distillation data, and explicit evaluation for robustness, long-tail behavior, and fairness. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable, task-aware system and adopt multi-stage, data‑aware, and privacy-conscious techniques to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature has expanded beyond soft-label matching to include intermediate representation imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and adaptive-teacher schemes, data- and domain-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when distillation helps, how teacher quality and data regimes affect outcomes, and what practical trade-offs remain. Open problems center on robustness to domain shift and adversaries, distillation without original data, and automated, architecture-agnostic pipelines for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language tasks. KD encompasses a family of transfer signals—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure—and is typically combined with data strategies (original, augmented, or synthesized data) and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but outcomes depend on choices of distillation targets, student capacity, data provenance, and teacher quality. Effective deployment adapts KD to task constraints, often integrating pretraining, multi-stage distillation, or multi-teacher schedules; outstanding challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases (notably on rare tokens), domain shift, and privacy or federated heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task‑Aware, Integrated Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical engine for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and adapted to task constraints—what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data limitations—KD routinely yields strong tradeoffs between efficiency and performance. However, its benefits are conditional: student capacity, data heterogeneity, teacher artifacts, and robustness or privacy constraints limit outcomes unless KD is combined with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data synthesis) and applied with deliberate, task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central engineering paradigm for converting large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft‑target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate features, relational statistics, and training dynamics, and that can operate in standard, online, federated, or data‑free regimes. When combined with architecture‑aware design, pretraining, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization), KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, its success depends on careful task‑aware choices: what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch, teacher artifacts, and rare‑case degradation. This synthesis summarizes core methods, practical tradeoffs, known failure modes, and recommended pipeline elements for reliable KD in vision and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into compact students to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a composable system—selecting appropriate distillation signals, matching architectures or mapping layers, managing data (including synthetic or data-free inputs), and combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving most of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, domain shift, and robustness or fairness is required. A practical stance treats KD as the central element of a broader compression pipeline, guided by task-aware signal design and rigorous evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deploying high-performing deep models under resource constraints by transferring information from large teacher models into smaller students. Approaches range from task-agnostic distillation and architecture search to layer-matching, internal representation imitation, data-free distillation, and techniques that adapt either the teacher or the student to improve transfer. Empirical work across vision and language shows these methods can substantially reduce model size and latency while retaining much of the original performance, and task- or domain-aware strategies often yield the best practical trade-offs. Remaining challenges include robustness without access to original data, aligning heterogeneous inputs or modalities, and automating compression for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi‑ingredient approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The KD toolkit includes softened-output (logit) supervision, intermediate representation and attention matching, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data strategies that range from augmentation to data-free synthesis. When integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful teacher–student design and data selection, KD often produces compact models that recover most of the teacher’s performance. Remaining limitations arise from capacity mismatch, limited or private data, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and sensitivity to domain shift and rare-token behaviors; practical pipelines therefore favor multi-objective distillation, tailored data strategies, and explicit robustness or privacy interventions.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are mature, diverse strategies to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their task performance. Approaches span architecture-level methods that search or prune for compact student networks, training-time methods that transfer dark knowledge via logits or intermediate representations, and data-centric methods that operate when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows success compressing large language models into lightweight networks for NLP tasks, highlights task- and data-specific pitfalls (notably for low-frequency tokens in sequence tasks), and motivates specialized extensions in federated and domain-adaptive settings. Theory and interpretive analyses have begun to clarify why distillation helps generalization and optimization, and recent work advocates shaping teachers to be more student-friendly or designing student-aware compression procedures. Overall, the literature shows a practical toolkit of complementary techniques—task-adaptive architecture search, feature- and attention-based matching, adversarial or synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-student co-training—each with trade-offs between efficiency, robustness, and fidelity to teacher behavior.

papers_seen.author: Hughes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened teacher logits to a toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention transfer, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-aware and data-free protocols, and combinations with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and student pretraining. KD is most effective when treated as the central component of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline that aligns distillation signals to student capacity, uses appropriate data strategies, and explicitly evaluates robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior. Remaining challenges include handling capacity mismatch, domain shift, privacy or data scarcity, and preserving rare-token or long‑tail behaviors under compression.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing models to smaller, efficient models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature has diversified beyond simple teacher→student logit-matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, online and federated protocols, teacher-free and data-free variants, and architectural co-design. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D perception, and NLP demonstrates that carefully chosen distillation signals, layer mappings, and training practices (e.g., pretraining, projected feature matching, selective sample weighting) produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance; remaining challenges include data heterogeneity, privacy, robustness, and automating teacher–student pairing and signal selection.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Research has produced a rich set of mechanisms (soft-targets, representation- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives), data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, and data-free surrogates), and complementary compression steps (pruning, architecture search, quantization). Empirical evidence shows that KD frequently recovers most teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on careful teacher–student design, data choices, and addressing capacity, optimization, and robustness limits.

papers_seen.author: Blankenship
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for producing compact models from larger teachers across deep learning and natural language processing. Treated as a design‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD transfers different kinds of information (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), adapts to constrained data regimes (including data‑free or synthesized data), and composes with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to produce deployable students. Its empirical success depends on careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity, thoughtful data and training curricula, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare‑case behavior, and fairness. Persistent failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and sensitivity to distribution shift—mean KD is most reliable when embedded in an integrated compression pipeline and tuned to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has grown beyond soft-target matching to include representation-level and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, meta-learned teachers, and data-aware or data-free protocols. Combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD forms a practical core of modern compression pipelines. However, success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity and data availability, and on addressing failure modes like capacity mismatch, domain shift, and transfer of teacher biases. Emerging best practices emphasize pretraining compact students, careful selection or synthesis of distillation data, adaptive teacher strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Conditional Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical framework for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance when combined with thoughtful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data and optimization; however, it has predictable failure modes that require complementary methods and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in NLP: Capabilities, Extensions, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning models for NLP and related domains. When combined with complementary strategies—pretraining of compact models, layer-matching techniques, targeted data augmentation, robustness-aware objectives, privacy-aware protocols, and adaptive teacher training—distillation can produce small models that retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of KD variants and complementary compression techniques enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and data-availability constraints. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers much of teacher performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints; however, practical pipelines must manage trade-offs and persistent gaps in robustness, domain-shift handling, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention- or relation-based objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware approaches including data-free or synthetic-data distillation. In practice KD is usually integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and task-aware training schedules to meet latency, memory, privacy, and robustness constraints. While KD often yields strong empirical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy, its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and nature of distillation data, and specific optimization choices; these dependencies motivate hybrid pipelines and targeted remedies for capacity mismatch, domain shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so the students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining most of the teacher’s utility. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational signals; they are commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design/search) and data strategies (use of original data, augmentation, or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows KD yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities when applied as a task-aware pipeline element, but its reliability depends on careful teacher–student alignment, choice of distillation targets, data preparation, and validation for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Crawford
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for producing compact models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a multi-signal toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational structure, and that can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data-free and synthetic-data methods). KD often recovers most of a teacher's performance while yielding substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but its effectiveness is context-dependent: it is limited by student capacity, data availability and domain match, propagation of teacher errors or rare-token failures, and robustness/privacy concerns. Practical success arises when KD is treated as an adaptive, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline that aligns signals, architectures, and data procedures to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Work across NLP and broader deep learning has developed multiple KD paradigms—soft-label (logit) matching, intermediate-representation matching, layer-to-layer and many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher aggregation, and data-free distillation—and combined KD with other compression methods such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. Empirical results show that well-designed distillation can yield compact models that approach the accuracy of large pre-trained models while offering substantial savings in parameters, latency, and computational cost. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, coping with limited or unavailable training data, and selecting or weighting multiple teachers per example. The literature suggests principled strategies—attention-based layer fusion, representation-level losses, teacher confidence or dynamic weighting, and synthetic-data generation—that mitigate these issues and enable effective deployment of compressed models in domain-specific and resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in vision, speech, and NLP. KD includes matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, and conveying relational or structural signals; it is often combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. The effectiveness of KD depends on deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity and architectural alignment, the distillation data regime (original, augmented, or synthesized), and training schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, or self-distillation). While KD routinely yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs, it has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, propagated teacher errors or biases, and degraded long-tail or out-of-distribution behavior—so reliable deployment treats KD as the starting point of a holistic, task-aware compression pipeline that incorporates complementary techniques and explicit robustness and evaluation practices.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Success depends on choosing appropriate distillation strategies that account for model structure, task specificity, data availability, and training dynamics. When tailored—via structural transformations, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer alignment, or data-centric augmentations—distillation consistently produces compact models that approach teacher accuracy and enable real-world use cases that would otherwise be impractical.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of task performance. The field encompasses softened-logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, online and multi-teacher schemes, data-free or data-limited techniques, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery. Empirical work shows KD often improves deployment trade-offs in vision, speech, and language tasks, but its reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and nature of distillation data, and interventions to mitigate optimization, robustness, and fairness issues. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a composable toolkit—selecting objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to match task and deployment constraints—and continue to explore theory and methods that address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals) and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on deliberate design choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, which data (real, augmented, or synthetic) to use, and how to mitigate harms such as transferred bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When integrated into a task-aware pipeline—combining pretraining, multi-level distillation objectives, projector/mapper layers, and data-side interventions—KD frequently yields students that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single training trick into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational or structural knowledge; it can be adapted to constraints such as missing training data, privacy, distributed training, and domain shifts; and when combined with complementary techniques (architecture adaptation, pruning, task-aware layer selection) it produces compact models that retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical use of KD requires matching the distillation strategy to the application constraints (what to transfer, which data to use, and how to align heterogeneous architectures).

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD is effective across modalities and tasks, from question answering and speech recognition to vision and federated learning, but its success depends on careful handling of teacher imperfections, data artifacts, and deployment constraints. Best practices include using multi-teacher or staged distillation, blending soft and hard targets, engineering teacher-student interfaces (e.g., projectors or student-aware teachers), and combining KD with complementary techniques such as quantization or federated momentum. When these strategies are applied thoughtfully, KD enables high-quality compact models suitable for real-world, resource-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modality-agnostic approach for producing compact models that meet deployment constraints. Treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of a teacher's performance when combined with appropriate data strategies, student initialization, and complementary compression methods. Successful distillation requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and domain behavior. I argue that KD should be adopted as the core component of compression pipelines, paired with principled pre-training of students, ensemble or adapted teachers where helpful, and data-aware or data-free procedures to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical, Conditional Endorsement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are indispensable tools for deploying high-capacity deep models in resource- and latency-constrained settings. When combined with architecture-aware strategies, task adaptation, and data-aware protocols, KD recovers much of teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and size reductions. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: optimization difficulties, domain and low-frequency token mismatches, privacy or data-availability constraints, and fairness concerns require tailored remedies. Effective compression thus integrates KD with architecture search, progressive replacement, data-free methods, and fairness- and federated-aware training to achieve reliable, deployable students.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Complementary Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal representations across many tasks and modalities, enabling substantial reductions in parameters and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not sufficient by itself in all settings: its success depends on what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases or errors. For robust, deployable compression, KD should be treated as the central element of a broader pipeline that includes data synthesis or augmentation, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or progressive module replacement), plus careful attention to privacy, fairness, and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated not as a single training trick but as the central, configurable engine of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When designed as a modular system that selects which teacher signals to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or channel signals, relational structure), aligns teacher and student architectures, and composes with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis), KD routinely produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its practical success requires careful handling of capacity mismatch, data availability (including data-free scenarios), teacher imperfections, and the preservation of robustness and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Methods span data-dependent distillation using teacher soft targets and intermediate hints, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, many-to-many layer mapping for large pre-trained language models, data-free or zero-shot distillation where training data are unavailable, and approaches that combine distillation with quantization or pruning for deployment. Empirical results demonstrate that distillation can recover much of a teacher's accuracy while enabling efficiency gains, but trade-offs remain around robustness, optimization difficulty, domain shifts, and the need for careful alignment of inputs or representations. Recent work addresses these challenges with generative replay, adversarial objectives, layer-matching distances, and teacher-annealing strategies, yet open problems include theory of optimization, scalable privacy-preserving protocols, and balancing fairness or robustness with compression.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation condenses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. A rich family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and data-free or federated variants—have been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture design to produce compact models that often retain much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on the choice of distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, availability and quality of data (or synthetic alternatives), and complementary training or architectural strategies. Key limitations remain around robustness, fairness, domain shift, and principled teacher selection, and ongoing work targets federated and privacy-sensitive settings as well as methods that pre-train compact students before distillation.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a practical, multimodal toolkit that reliably shrinks large models into deployable students while preserving much of their utility. When treated as the central component of compression pipelines and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD delivers substantial gains in latency, memory, and communication efficiency. However, safe and effective use of KD requires careful, task-aware choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle data scarcity or privacy limits, and how to combine distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or student pretraining. This paper argues KD should be the default engine for model compression in deep learning and NLP, outlines its key mechanisms, highlights practical limitations and failure modes, and provides concrete recommendations for robust, deployed KD pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure; when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data and architecture strategies, KD yields deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success with KD is conditional—dependent on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and optimization—but treating KD as an integrated, task-aware pipeline provides reliable pathways to efficient models while highlighting concrete failure modes that require targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the default core technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure when its signals, data, and optimization are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD must be applied as a system-level, design-sensitive pipeline—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, privacy-aware procedures, and complementary compression primitives—to avoid optimization failures, capacity mismatch, and propagation of teacher errors. I recommend KD-first workflows that explicitly plan for data, evaluation under shift, and targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. A rich set of techniques—soft-target (logit) transfer, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive replacement, data-free or zero-shot distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—has emerged. Practical success depends on choices about teacher signals, student architecture and capacity, data availability and augmentation, and integration with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and rare behaviors, and operating under limited or private data.
