papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible tool for compressing large deep learning models into deployable students. Recent work shows KD can both directly reduce model size and serve as a mechanism to transfer inductive biases, intermediate representations, and task-specific attention. However, real-world constraints — limited or private training data, domain and client heterogeneity, and redundant teacher representations — require KD methods that are data-free, adversarially robust, task-aware, and selective about what teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modular approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a configurable pipeline—choosing what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to supply or synthesize distillation data—KD routinely yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: student capacity, data provenance or availability, teacher quality, and robustness/fairness concerns limit naïve application. Responsible deployment therefore requires combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), careful teacher–student alignment, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, low-frequency token degradation, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted training paradigm for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behaviour and representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise imitation, attention- or relation-aware objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and a spectrum of data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). In practice, KD is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline—combined with pre-training, pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, open problems remain around robustness, preservation of rare behaviors, teacher-induced errors, privacy, and principled teacher–student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

KD routinely yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data availability, and task constraints. At the same time, KD has clear limits—capacity mismatch, teacher artifacts, distributional shift, and privacy or data-availability concerns—that require careful pipeline design and validation for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal training paradigm that compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD methods—ranging from softened-output matching to layer- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-free strategies—are effective components of practical compression pipelines. Success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, managing data availability (including synthesized or privacy-sensitive approaches), and combining KD with complementary compression primitives to balance efficiency, accuracy, and robustness. Remaining challenges include principled teacher selection, capacity and representation mismatch, preservation of long-tail or rare behaviors, and reliable robustness and fairness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. A broad repertoire of KD techniques transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate-feature or attention matching, and relational or layer-wise alignment, and these techniques are commonly combined with data augmentation, teacher schedules, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distributional match, and optimization protocols. Best practice treats KD as a flexible toolkit to be adapted to deployment constraints rather than a single fixed recipe; key open challenges include theoretical understanding, robust distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and preserving fairness and rare-behavior fidelity during compression.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A diverse toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational or ensemble signals, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies (including data-free synthesis). KD is typically composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student design to meet latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. While KD regularly yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability and provenance, alignment of signals, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Schmitt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most productively framed not as a single heuristic but as a configurable, task-aware component of model-compression pipelines. When practitioners treat KD as a multi-signal workflow—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure), aligning teacher and student capacity and architecture, and combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or federated protocols)—it reliably produces compact, deployable models that recover much of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its benefits depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including data-free and federated regimes), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional shift. Responsible deployment therefore requires designing KD as part of a broader engineering pipeline with targeted evaluation and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from soft-target logit matching into a multifaceted, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD methods transfer outputs, internal representations, relational structure, or ensemble behavior and are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis or privacy-aware protocols to meet deployment constraints. Successful application depends on matching distillation targets and training data to student capacity and task structure while addressing teacher imperfections, domain shift, and privacy or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, multi-signal approach for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) while retaining much of task performance. KD operates through softened outputs, intermediate representation and attention matching, relational objectives, and multi- or self-distillation schedules. It integrates naturally with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and can be adapted for domain-specific or modality-specific requirements. Practical success requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to distillation data provenance (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and mitigation strategies for capacity mismatch, robustness, and bias transfer. Remaining research priorities include principled teacher selection, reliable data-free distillation, stability for low-capacity students, and safeguards for fairness and out-of-distribution behavior.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practical Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of training techniques that transfer information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving predictive performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, transferring relational structure among examples or channels, multi- and self-distillation, and data-aware protocols including data-free and domain-adaptive approaches. Its practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and task constraints, handling data availability and privacy, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques. While KD often yields deployable students that retain much of teacher utility, important limitations remain around domain shift, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and robustness to rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression (and When to Combine It)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact deep and NLP models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD delivers consistent accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across modalities, improves small-model representations, and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not always sufficient on its own: success requires careful choice of transfer signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity and architecture, and integration with complementary compression, data, or training procedures to preserve rare or safety-critical behaviors. I argue that KD should be treated as the central element of a compression toolkit, applied pragmatically with domain- and deployment-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Model Compression: A Conditional, Task‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across multiple signals—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure—and composes naturally with complementary compression methods. Its practical value is that it often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory, and deployability. At the same time, KD is not a universal solution: success depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, availability and provenance of distillation data, and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors. Therefore KD should be treated as the default core of a task-aware compression pipeline that explicitly mitigates known failure modes through signal selection, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for turning large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD operates by transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational statistics, and can be combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). When used in task-aware pipelines and matched to student capacity and data constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve a substantial fraction of teacher performance; however, its success is conditional on careful teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare-case behaviors, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Davies
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller ‘‘student’’ models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so students can meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. A rich spectrum of KD methods exists — from soft-target (logit) matching to representation- and attention-level supervision, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or federated variants — and KD is typically combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows well-designed distillation pipelines frequently recover most of a teacher’s performance in language and other modalities, but success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality and calibration, choice of distilled signals, data availability, and careful optimization; open challenges include robustness, rare-token/long-tail behaviors, propagation of teacher errors and biases, and principled data-free or privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core method for producing compact, deployable models from large neural teachers. KD is effective across modalities and tasks because it can transfer multiple forms of information—soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure—and because it composes well with other compression primitives. At the same time, KD has important limits (capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and teacher imperfections) that require task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and whether to synthesize or privatize data. Best practice treats KD as a flexible toolkit: select distillation signals and data strategies to match deployment constraints, combine KD with pruning/quantization where helpful, and explicitly evaluate robustness and rare-case fidelity before production use.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and language tasks. Modern KD is a flexible toolkit that transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure), composes with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design), and must be adapted to data availability, student capacity, and deployment constraints. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in production settings, its reliability depends on careful teacher–student design, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and degradation under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression methods form a diverse toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. Research spans soft-label and self-distillation strategies, layer- and representation-level transfers, architecture-aware and task-adaptive compression, and deployment-aware approaches that combine pruning, quantization, and distillation. Empirical work shows that careful choice of distillation signal (logits, intermediate representations, or feature maps), alignment strategy between teacher and student layers, data augmentation, and optimization scheduling materially affects student performance. Practical systems exploit these design choices to compress large pre-trained language models, accelerate inference, enable heterogeneous-device training, or improve low-precision networks. Despite progress, open questions remain about principled objective design, sample efficiency under limited data, and theory connecting transferred representations to generalization.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for turning large, high‑performing neural networks into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment under memory, latency, data, and privacy constraints. A range of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure), alignment strategies (layer-wise matching, attention-mediated projection, task-aware filtering), and training regimes (multi-teacher ensembles, online/self-distillation, or adversarial setups) have been developed to trade off compression with retained performance. Across modalities, well-designed distillation pipelines—often combined with complementary compression methods or student pretraining—yield compact models that approach teacher accuracy while enabling real-world use cases that would otherwise be impractical.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Engine of Practical Model Compression: A Task‑aware, Integrated Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high‑leverage approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD offers multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational maps) and works across different data regimes (real, augmented, synthesized, or data‑free). However, KD alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, privacy, or optimal compression; reliable deployment requires pairing KD with task‑aware student preparation, representation‑level objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). This paper argues KD should be treated as the central engine of compression pipelines but only as part of an integrated, context‑sensitive workflow that explicitly addresses capacity mismatch, data provenance, and failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining task performance. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has grown from soft-label matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation alignment, relational and attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free methods). Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, student capacity and pretraining, data availability or synthesis, and how KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Important open issues include handling heterogenous data and architectures, preserving robustness and rare-behavior performance, and operating under privacy or federated constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ho
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central but Conditional Engine of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large pretrained models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely recovers much of teacher performance while enabling reductions in latency, memory, and privacy exposure, but its reliability depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, student and teacher design, and distillation data. For production-grade compression, KD should be treated as the default starting point in a hybrid pipeline that combines representation-aware transfer with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with explicit evaluation of robustness, long-tail behavior, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Bauer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students so that systems meet latency, memory, energy, or privacy constraints while retaining most of the teacher’s utility. KD methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate features or attention, and transferring relational or contrastive signals; they are commonly combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design/search) and with data-side strategies ranging from fidelity-preserving augmentation to fully data-free synthesis. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but its reliability depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance or synthesis strategy, and careful evaluation for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a task-aware component of a broader compression and evaluation workflow.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central tool for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teachers to smaller, deployable students. When KD is designed as a system—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—it delivers large practical wins in latency, memory, and deployability while preserving most task performance. Responsible use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a multifunctional, task-aware toolkit that should sit at the center of model-compression pipelines. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and guided by careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to manage data, KD routinely yields compact models suitable for deployment; however, realizing those gains requires explicit handling of robustness, bias propagation, capacity mismatch, and limited-data scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade‑offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, ranking, and reading-comprehension tasks, practitioners use softened output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, multi- and self-teaching schedules, and data-aware or data-free procedures. KD is most effective when distillation signals, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen together and when KD is combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Important open problems include closing capacity and optimization gaps, avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases, preserving robustness under domain or adversarial shifts, and designing principled teacher selection and data-synthesis strategies.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Necessarily Integrated into a Broader Compression Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for converting large, high-performance deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers substantial parameter and latency savings while preserving much of teacher performance, but its reliability depends on engineering choices about what to transfer, how to prepare teachers and students, data provenance and augmentation, and complementary compression methods. Responsible production use therefore treats KD as the core of a system-level compression pipeline—combined with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted evaluations for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific behavior—rather than as a standalone remedy.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a flexible paradigm that improves efficiency, robustness, privacy, and generalization across modalities and tasks. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight deployable models, transfer internal representations to preserve teacher behaviors, operate without original training data, and be adapted to distributed and privacy-sensitive settings. Recent methodological advances—layer- and attention-aware projection, multi-teacher schedules, meta-learned teachers, and techniques connecting KD to regularization—make distillation a practical and theoretically grounded tool for both research and production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile mechanism to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and matched to task constraints, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Success with KD depends on deliberate choices about what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or missing teacher data, and how to protect robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be the default compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP systems, but its safe and effective use requires task-aware design and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with complementary methods such as student pretraining, progressive replacement, data synthesis, and fairness- or privacy-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Li
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of task performance. A coherent body of work frames KD as a toolkit: matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention/relational structure, ensembling or multi-teacher transfers, and operating across data regimes from plentiful labeled data to fully data-free or privacy-constrained settings. KD is often composed with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation; real-world success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, managing data mismatch or scarcity, and explicitly validating robustness, calibration, and long-tail behavior. Remaining challenges include principled teacher–student alignment for heterogeneous architectures, reliable distillation without original data, and preserving fairness and rare-event behavior under compression.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core—but Conditional—Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, appropriate data strategies, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely delivers strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. However, its effectiveness is conditional on clear engineering choices: what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to provision or synthesize data, and how to evaluate and mitigate harms such as propagated biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and weakened robustness. A production-ready stance treats KD as the default engine for compression but couples it with targeted remedies for its known limitations.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger, higher-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Across NLP and broader deep-learning tasks, a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Distillation is both a practical engineering toolkit for deployment constraints (latency, memory, heterogeneity, privacy) and an active research area that raises challenges around preserving robustness, handling domain and data shifts, and designing principled curricula and teacher signals for maximal downstream utility.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for transferring useful behavior from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets and protocols—soft-target/logit matching, representation- and attention-level imitation, relational or correlation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data strategies that range from using original training data to augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols. KD is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that aligns student capacity and architecture with chosen signals and augments distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and degraded out-of-domain or long-tail behavior; addressing these requires targeted algorithmic, data, and evaluation advances.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques compress large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behaviors and internal structure so compact models can meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The KD toolkit includes matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention patterns, multi-teacher and online paradigms, data-aware or data-free strategies, and integration with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware search. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, preparing students (pretraining or staged schedules), shaping distillation data (augmentation or synthesis), and combining KD with complementary compression primitives. Remaining challenges include reliably preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases or vulnerabilities, handling heterogeneous architecture alignment, and achieving robustness under distribution shift or data scarcity.

KD routinely yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline, but its success is conditional on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, the provenance and quality of distillation data, and mitigation of propagated teacher errors or biases. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as the core of a task-aware workflow that composes with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and explicit robustness and fairness checks.

papers_seen.author: Cunningham
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically effective family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Modern KD extends beyond softened-output matching to include feature- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation schedules, data-aware and data-free protocols, and combinations with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical evidence shows KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities when practitioners attend to teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, and data strategies; remaining challenges center on domain shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts, and reliable distillation without original data.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and accelerates large neural models by transferring information from one or more teacher models into a smaller student. Across vision and language, KD variants extend from logit-matching to feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher ensembling, online/co-distillation, privacy-aware and federated setups, and combinations with quantization or structured pruning. Practical pipelines combine KD with architecture-aware transformations, domain adaptation, and task-specific pretraining to obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Despite empirical success across modalities and deployment settings, trade-offs remain in teacher selection, information type to transfer, stability for heterogeneous architectures, and theoretical interpretation of what is transferred; these motivate further research into adaptive teacher weighting, feature alignment layers, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation for real-world systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at multiple levels (outputs, intermediate representations, relations). Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a toolbox that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and augmentation-driven protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data strategy, and optimization; when integrated into a broader compression pipeline, KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include reliably preserving rare or out-of-domain behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases or errors, and operating under data- or privacy-constrained regimes.

Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but outcomes depend on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher quality, and distributional robustness; addressing these requires deliberate pipeline design and evaluation targeted to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of practical and theoretical approaches for shrinking deep models while retaining performance. Methods span logits-based soft-label transfer, layer- and feature-level matching, architecture-aware transformations, teacher improvement or selection strategies, data-free and privacy-preserving pipelines, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural teacher models into smaller, deployable students. A mature set of methods transfers information at multiple levels — softened outputs, internal features or attention maps, relational statistics, and multi-teacher or online schedules — and is commonly combined with data-side strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free approaches) and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical evidence shows KD routinely produces compact models that recover much of teacher performance when pipelines are designed to match student capacity, training data availability, and task constraints; however, predictable failure modes and open problems remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, robustness and long-tail behavior, and privacy-sensitive or data-free settings.

papers_seen.author: Gallagher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Conditional Engine of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for producing compact models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, internal representations, attention or relational signals) and, when integrated with complementary compression techniques and careful data and architecture choices, routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher quality, and robustness or fairness requirements shape outcomes. Treating KD as the central element of a deliberate, task-aware compression pipeline—rather than as a standalone cure—gives the most reliable route to deployable, high-performing compact models.

papers_seen.author: Key
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modality-agnostic technique that, when embedded in a task-aware compression pipeline, yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is powerful but conditional: its success depends on student capacity, choice of distilled signals, data provenance (including data-free options), and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift failure modes. Treating KD as a central, composable tool—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and careful evaluation—produces the most reliable deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been widely adopted to reduce model size and runtime while retaining performance. Work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows multiple complementary strategies—logit matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and self-distillation—can be effective alone or in combination. Practical success depends on choices about teacher strength, student architecture, pre-training, and optimization, and recent systems integrate distillation with pruning, low-precision, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD methods range from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher and meta-learned teacher schemes, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical deployment requires careful choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to prepare and align students, and how to handle data limitations, distributional shift, and robustness. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance at dramatically reduced cost, persistent gaps (capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, rare-token and adversarial robustness) motivate hybrid pipelines and targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Curtis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models so compact systems meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When treated as a configurable pipeline—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and shaping the distillation data—distillation routinely yields efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, its benefits are conditional: success depends on student capacity, data provenance, signal choice, and robustness evaluation; naive application risks propagating teacher errors, amplifying biases, or degrading rare-token and out-of-domain behavior. Practical deployment therefore combines distillation with complementary compression primitives and targeted engineering to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD is effective across modalities and tasks, from question answering and speech recognition to vision and federated learning, but its success depends on careful handling of teacher imperfections, data artifacts, and deployment constraints. Best practices include using multi-teacher or staged distillation, blending soft and hard targets, engineering teacher-student interfaces (e.g., projectors or student-aware teachers), and combining KD with complementary techniques such as quantization or federated momentum. When these strategies are applied thoughtfully, KD enables high-quality compact models suitable for real-world, resource-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Practical, and Best Used as an Integrated, Multi‑Level Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works best when it goes beyond naive logits-only matching and integrates representation-level transfer, input-side interventions, robustness-aware objectives, and complementary compression methods. However, effective deployment requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to data provenance and augmentation, explicit handling of teacher uncertainty and bias, and privacy-aware training choices. Treated as a flexible, multi-stage pipeline rather than a single recipe, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while managing the key failure modes that emerge in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large models (teachers) to smaller models (students). Treated as a central component of compression pipelines and adapted to task constraints, KD can produce compact, deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Effective application requires careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to manage data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques. Persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors, and avoidance of transferred biases or robustness regressions; addressing these motivates hybrid, task-aware engineering and further research into evaluation and theory.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal training paradigm that compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD methods—ranging from softened-output matching to layer- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-free strategies—are effective components of practical compression pipelines. Success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, managing data availability (including synthesized or privacy-sensitive approaches), and combining KD with complementary compression primitives to balance efficiency, accuracy, and robustness. Remaining challenges include principled teacher selection, capacity and representation mismatch, preservation of long-tail or rare behaviors, and reliable robustness and fairness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. Over the past decade these methods have evolved from logits-based soft-label transfer to a wide range of strategies including feature- and attention-matching, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols, and adaptations for few-shot or federated settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines can retain much of teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and inference cost; however, effectiveness depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and practical constraints such as privacy, communication, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides a rich set of transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and composes naturally with architecture search, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success is conditional on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher quality, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be treated as the default, configurable first-line technique in compression pipelines, but only when combined with task-aware choices and complementary methods that mitigate its predictable failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression: when applied as an integrated, task-aware system it enables compact students that preserve much of a teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware surgery), careful data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols), and explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment and robustness evaluation. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits are conditional on signal selection, data and initialization choices, and evaluation for fairness and domain-shift resilience. I argue for treating KD as a configurable pipeline (signals, data, architecture, optimization) and for adopting specific practices that mitigate common failure modes in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When applied as a design-sensitive pipeline—choosing appropriate transfer signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, managing or synthesizing distillation data, and combining distillation with other compression primitives—KD routinely delivers strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, its practical success is conditional on student capacity, data availability, teacher quality, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors; therefore KD should be the default starting point for compression but must be integrated into broader, task-aware workflows to be reliable in production.
