papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing deep models and transferring capabilities across architectures and modalities. KD has enabled large speedups and model-size reductions while preserving or even improving downstream task performance when carefully applied. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and distributional heterogeneity, and it can transmit teacher biases or errors. Combining logit-based supervision with feature- and relation-focused objectives, aligning intermediate representations, and adapting distillation strategies to task and data constraints yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Mack
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach for producing compact models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD encompasses multiple transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure) and is commonly combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data‑free protocols). Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, and other modalities shows that, when carefully matched to student capacity, architecture, and data regime, KD yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, KD has predictable limits—student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and transfer of teacher errors or biases—that require task‑aware pipeline design, evaluation for robustness and fairness, and combinations with other compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression, Regularization, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a flexible, multi-purpose methodology rather than only a compression trick. KD enables smaller, efficient models for deployment, but it also serves as a mechanism for learned regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release. Practical success relies on matching the distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), the teacher selection and scheduling, and the data or data-generation strategy to the deployment constraints. Combining logits-based supervision with representation-level objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware query mechanisms produces more reliable and robust student models for real-world NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single recipe for copying teacher logits into a central, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and behaviors of larger teachers. KD methods vary in what they transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational structure), how they handle data availability (data-rich, data-free, federated), and how they combine with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments select and tune KD components to match modality, data-privacy constraints, and latency or memory budgets.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or costly neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A convergent literature shows a spectrum of distillation objectives (soft-targets, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), a set of practical integrations with pruning, quantization and architecture search, and a set of recurring challenges: teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or unavailable distillation data, and robustness under domain shift or adversarial influence. Effective pipelines attend to student initialization (including pre-training), careful choice of distilled signals and layer mappings, and targeted data strategies (augmentation or synthetic data) to achieve deployable compressed models while managing performance, fairness and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied compression techniques have become central tools for reducing the computational and storage cost of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Research has expanded beyond the original soft-label paradigm to include distillation of internal representations, layer- and channel-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and teacher-student co-design. Applications span vision, NLP, graph models, generative networks, and large-scale distributed training. Recent work also explores distillation for robustness, low-precision deployment, few-shot compression, and federated or multi-device settings. Despite strong empirical gains, open challenges remain in transferring inductive biases, choosing what and when to distill, and preserving attributes such as fairness and adversarial robustness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Integrated Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central component of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it offers a flexible set of mechanisms that reliably reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when applied as a modular, task-aware system—combining soft-target matching, intermediate-representation transfer, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Its practical success depends on deliberate teacher–student co-design, matching transferred signals to student capacity, and explicit remedies for data scarcity, capacity mismatch, and propagated teacher errors; when integrated with these safeguards, KD delivers deployable, efficient models across domains.

papers_seen.author: Sampson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring learned behavior at multiple levels (output distributions, intermediate representations, relational structure). Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, and which data strategies to use (original data, synthesized surrogates, or data‑free generation). Remaining challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving rare-token or domain‑specific behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and integrating KD with pruning, quantization, or federated and hardware‑heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power from larger, high-capacity models (teachers or ensembles) into smaller, efficient models (students) while preserving accuracy and generalization. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (logits) to imitating intermediate representations, designing student-friendly teachers, handling limited or no access to original training data, and tailoring distillation to task-specific architectures (e.g., detection, reinforcement learning, recommender systems). Practical concerns include privacy, computational cost at training or inference, multi-teacher integration, and the role of pre-training for compact models. Empirical results across vision, language evaluation, medical imaging, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning show that appropriately chosen distillation objectives and training regimes can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while delivering large savings in storage and latency.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of task performance. The field encompasses softened-logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, online and multi-teacher schemes, data-free or data-limited techniques, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery. Empirical work shows KD often improves deployment trade-offs in vision, speech, and language tasks, but its reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and nature of distillation data, and interventions to mitigate optimization, robustness, and fairness issues. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a composable toolkit—selecting objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to match task and deployment constraints—and continue to explore theory and methods that address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Allen

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning models for NLP and related domains. When combined with complementary strategies—pretraining of compact models, layer-matching techniques, targeted data augmentation, robustness-aware objectives, privacy-aware protocols, and adaptive teacher training—distillation can produce small models that retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ponce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Conditional Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central, task-aware component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, task-adaptive design), KD routinely produces favorable trade-offs between efficiency and retained capability. Its success is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, availability and provenance of distillation data, and choices about which signals to transfer determine outcomes. Responsible use of KD therefore requires task-aware signal selection, data strategies for scarce or private data, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness in deployment contexts.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relationships. Methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate features or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when originals are unavailable, and designing architecture-aware layer mappings. KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and used across modalities (vision, language, generative models) to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and propagation of biases.

papers_seen.title: What Is Known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When paired with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware choices about data and training schedules, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distributional shift, and operating effectively with limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Vasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Conditional Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted technique for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, and privacy constraints. As KD has diversified beyond simple logit matching into feature-level, relational, adversarial, and data-free variants, it functions best when treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware student design, complementary primitives (pruning, quantization), and careful data and evaluation strategies. KD often preserves much of teacher utility, but its reliability is conditional on student capacity, data availability and quality, teacher quality, and explicit robustness and fairness evaluation. A task-aware, multi-signal KD workflow—combining soft-targets, intermediate-feature imitation, data strategies (including synthesis or augmentation), and complementary compression—offers the most reliable route to deployable compressed models while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure; when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data and architecture strategies, KD yields deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success with KD is conditional—dependent on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and optimization—but treating KD as an integrated, task-aware pipeline provides reliable pathways to efficient models while highlighting concrete failure modes that require targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing smaller, faster models from large pretrained teachers. KD operates through multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and yields substantial efficiency gains when paired with complementary methods and task-aware design. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robustness, fairness, or optimal hardware utilization: achieving production-grade compression requires matching distillation objectives to data availability, architecture mismatch, privacy constraints, and combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the core of a multi-tool compression pipeline—central to practical deployment but reliant on deliberate system-level choices to realize its benefits reliably.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Evolving Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental and versatile approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. It enables compact, efficient student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, supports deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. Recent advances extend distillation beyond simple logits matching to many-to-many layer mapping, task-adaptive compression, teacher-aware training, adversarial and data-free scenarios, and robustness-aware objectives. Together these developments show that distillation is both a practical engineering tool and a rich research paradigm for addressing capacity, data availability, privacy, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ingram
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible set of transfer mechanisms that make it the natural centerpiece of model‑compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When treated as a task‑aware, design‑sensitive process and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or privacy‑aware protocols), KD routinely yields deployable students with strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs. However, KD is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, optimization sensitivity, and distribution‑shift or fairness failures persist. Practical success therefore requires explicit choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students, which data to use, and targeted remedies for robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level matching, data augmentation, selective sample strategies, and multi-teacher or federated adaptations—KD can produce efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD has known failure modes (teacher error propagation, data- and device-heterogeneity, and sample-wise regularization effects) that require explicit remedies and system-level design choices to ensure robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Pipelines, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Researchers frame KD as a configurable set of transfer mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational losses, and ensemble- or self-distillation—combined with data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic) and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Empirical evidence shows KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when student capacity, teacher quality, and data provenance are aligned; however, its success is conditional and requires design-aware pipelines and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and flexible mechanism for producing compact, deployable models across modalities. Treated as the central element of a compression pipeline, KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teachers into smaller students, and when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data strategies it routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest loss in task performance. However, KD alone is insufficient in many production settings: capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, data availability (including data-free methods), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior must all be addressed to produce reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students. A rich family of KD methods—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, data-free and data-augmented distillation, and teacher-student co-design—has been developed to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) across vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation objectives, data strategies, and architecture choices are well matched. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, scarcity or absence of real data, and preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models. Practical pipelines combine pretraining of compact architectures, multi-objective distillation (outputs + internals), data augmentation or synthesis, and teacher adaptation to produce robust, efficient student models.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While classic distillation focuses on matching teacher output probabilities, practical compression across modalities and tasks benefits from richer transfer mechanisms: aligning internal representations, selecting task-relevant signals, leveraging data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are scarce, and using adversarial or ensemble strategies to expose diverse and robust teacher knowledge. When combined thoughtfully these methods enable students that are much smaller and faster while retaining or even improving accuracy and robustness on downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Briggs
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, multi-signal toolkit for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and language tasks, KD can preserve much of teacher utility while reducing inference cost, memory use, and enabling on-device or low-latency deployment. Practical success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure), how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, and how to obtain or synthesize appropriate distillation data. KD works best when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and targeted evaluation to detect robustness, fairness, and domain-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring information from larger teachers to compact students. Across modalities and tasks, KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention transfer, relational objectives, and multi-teacher or online protocols. Practical KD is typically applied as part of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, or data strategies—to meet latency, memory, privacy, and robustness requirements. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance, success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity and task constraints and on addressing failure modes such as domain shift, rare-behavior degradation, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses information from large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The approach has diversified from soft-label matching into a toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or combinations thereof; it can be adapted to settings with limited or no access to original training data, and it is often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and integrating KD into a broader compression pipeline that validates robustness and fairness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond simple soft-target matching to include intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-limited or data-free approaches. When composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and guided by careful teacher–student co-design and data strategy, KD routinely yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance; however, practical limits remain related to capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and task- or architecture-specific challenges.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design‑Sensitive Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, design‑sensitive core of model compression for deep learning and NLP: it is a flexible set of transfer mechanisms that, when matched to student capacity, architecture, and data constraints and combined with complementary primitives, routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is a conditional rather than universal remedy — it introduces predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagated teacher artifacts, degraded long‑tail behavior, and fairness or robustness regressions) that require explicit mitigation, careful data strategies, and principled evaluation. A production‑ready stance treats KD as a central, configurable component of a broader compression workflow rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal suite of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The approach has evolved from matching softened logits to include intermediate-representation and attention/relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data strategies that range from using original training examples to synthetic or data-free generation. KD is most effective when treated as a task- and design-aware component of a broader compression pipeline that includes complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful handling of teacher–student capacity, data provenance, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior. Predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, degraded rare-token/long-tail performance, and sensitivity to distribution shift or limited data—motivate targeted mitigations such as intermediate feature alignment, student pretraining, multi-teacher or staged schedules, and hardware-aware compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Research over the past decade has produced a wide array of distillation variants (logit-based supervision, feature and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation, data-free methods) and shown how KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet practical constraints. Empirical and theoretical work identifies both the strengths of KD (regularization, practical deployment gains, domain adaptation) and its limits (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors), motivating a pragmatic set of design choices for robust compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention patterns, transferring relational structure, and employing multi- or self-distillation schedules. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about distillation data, teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware objectives. While KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs, its success is conditional on student capacity, data provenance, teacher quality, and robustness concerns; addressing these requires pipeline-minded, task-aware design and targeted interventions for long-tail behaviors, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning inputs and architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic samples, curriculum)—KD enables resource-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student; addressing these constraints through multi-teacher designs, black-box adaptation, and feature-level alignment remains essential for robust, private, and high-performance compression.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses the functionality of larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and NLP, KD variants—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, online and multi-teacher schemes, and task-adaptive architecture search—have enabled deployment of compact models with strong empirical performance while revealing trade-offs in teacher–student alignment, data availability, and robustness. Key open challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, effective data-free distillation, and preserving fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors during compression.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What is Known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Existing practice spans matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations or attention, online and ensemble distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches when original training data are unavailable. KD is typically combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and shaped by practical concerns—teacher–student capacity alignment, what and how to transfer, data availability or privacy, and robustness—which determine real-world effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task‑Aware Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood and applied as a configurable, task‑aware core of model compression pipelines rather than as a single recipe. Treated as a modular toolkit—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to align architectures—KD routinely produces compact students that recover much of teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques and explicit evaluation for robustness and rare‑case behaviors. Responsible deployment requires deliberate handling of capacity mismatch, data constraints, and propagated teacher artifacts through targeted adaptations such as multi‑teacher aggregation, data‑free or privacy‑aware protocols, and architecture‑aware student design.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central — but Conditional — Paradigm for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. Treated as a configurable pipeline that selects what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to source distillation data, KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. Its strengths are maximized when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful engineering; its limits appear when student capacity, data provenance, or teacher errors and biases are not explicitly handled. This paper argues KD should be the default starting point for compression while emphasizing principled design choices and safeguards to ensure robust, fair, and data-efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into compact, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure—and interoperates with complementary compression methods (pre-training of small models, architecture adaptation, pruning, and quantization). Practical deployment of KD requires matching the distillation signals and data strategy to student capacity and constraints (latency, memory, privacy, or heterogeneous architectures), deliberate handling of domain shift and low-frequency behaviors, and attention to teacher calibration or co-design. When these elements are chosen and tuned for the application, KD yields compact models that retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while meeting real-world resource and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Practical Model Compression: Conditional Strengths and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a modular core of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data synthesis), KD routinely produces substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness is conditional on design choices—what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how data are handled, and how capacity and robustness gaps are mitigated—so practitioners should adopt KD as a default starting point but tune objectives, data strategies, and complementary methods to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Dalton
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a flexible, central toolkit within model-compression pipelines. By transferring multiple types of signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure) and combining distillation with complementary techniques (student pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies), practitioners can produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate known failure modes such as capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, and robustness or fairness degradation.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. In practice KD is used alongside complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (pretraining, synthetic data, multi-stage schedules) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and can provide useful regularization, its success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data provenance, and safeguards against propagating teacher errors or biases. This synthesis summarizes common methods, practical considerations, representative applications, and recurring limitations to guide task-aware application of KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a multifaceted toolkit for shrinking large neural models while retaining much of their accuracy. Approaches include matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, transforming architectures to be resource-efficient, and designing teacher–student curricula or multi-teacher aggregations. KD is applied across supervised, self-supervised, few-shot, federated, and privacy-constrained scenarios and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and capacity, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; when designed carefully, KD enables deployment of compact models for diverse NLP and vision tasks while exposing open questions about robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD enables deployment under latency, storage, and privacy constraints by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals from teacher to student. When treated as a configurable toolkit — choosing which teacher signals to transfer, how to align representations, and which complementary compression methods to apply — distillation yields efficient models that are practical for real-world NLP and vision deployments.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD techniques include matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate features or attention patterns, and using multi- or self-distillation schedules; they are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet deployment constraints. KD has been effective across vision, language, speech, and retrieval tasks, but its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student. Practical pipelines therefore choose distillation signals and data strategies that suit the target task, and complement KD with additional compression and validation to mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, and brittleness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, composable approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an integrated, task-aware pipeline that selects which signals to transfer, aligns teacher and student architectures, and uses appropriate data strategies (including augmentation or synthesis), KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Its success is conditional on student capacity, data availability and quality, teacher reliability, and architecture alignment, so robust deployment requires complementary compression primitives and diagnostic procedures.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies aim to transfer predictive behavior from larger or more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more resource-efficient ones. The literature shows a variety of mechanisms (soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature alignment, progressive module replacement, adversarial feature matching), data- and training-focused interventions (data selection, augmentation, mixup, control of dataset complexity), and hybrid combinations with pruning or ensembling. Empirical results across NLP and vision tasks indicate that KD can preserve much of teacher performance while accelerating inference, but success depends strongly on (a) the choice of distillation targets and layer mappings, (b) the complexity and provenance of the distillation data, and (c) complementary techniques such as pre-training, feature-level matching, or structured pruning. Practical approaches therefore tailor the distillation recipe to model capacity, task characteristics, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted framework for transferring knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods span soft-label matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble transfers, and data-side strategies including augmentation and synthetic or data-free inputs. When integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance; however, practical use requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability, and distributional or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It operates through multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and is most effective when treated as a configurable, task- and data-aware toolkit rather than a single recipe. KD integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or public data) to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. Success depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to manage data and robustness trade-offs; addressing these systematically yields reliable compressed models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a diverse toolkit for transferring information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more constrained models. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, altering training curricula, and designing compression-aware teachers or architectures. These approaches have been applied across domains including vision, speech, translation, retrieval, and on-device deployment, and have been adapted to privacy- and communication-constrained settings. Empirical and analytical work has clarified different mechanisms by which distillation aids learning, and recent work explores automation, adversarial feature transfer, sample selection, and architecture-aware strategies to improve efficiency without sacrificing much performance.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can retain much of the performance of their teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to include feature- and layer-level supervision, online and multi-teacher schemes, meta-learned teachers, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical work shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost with modest performance loss, but success depends on careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Remaining practical issues include teacher–student heterogeneity, propagation of teacher errors, robustness to domain shifts, and limits to compression for some generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mendez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi‑ingredient approach that can serve as the core mechanism for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. Its strengths are broad—transferring softened outputs, internal representations, attention patterns, and relational signals—but its effectiveness is conditional. Realizing reliable, high-quality compression in practice requires matching distillation targets to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, integrating KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture design), and explicitly evaluating and mitigating robustness, fairness, and distribution‑shift failure modes. When KD is applied as a design‑sensitive pipeline element rather than a single recipe, it consistently yields favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across modalities and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Outcomes, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- and relation-aware objectives, multi- or self-distillation schedules, and data strategies that range from using original training data to synthetic or data-free generation. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, architecture, and deployment constraints. Empirically, well-designed distillation pipelines recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but common failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, sensitivity to data mismatch or scarcity, and degraded robustness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. The literature documents a spectrum of KD objectives (soft-output matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational losses), protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi-teacher, and teacher-free), and data strategies (original-data distillation, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can retain much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, but persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Flexible — but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods have matured into a practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. These techniques have been applied across domains (vision, speech, NLP, healthcare), settings (offline compression, federated learning, continual adaptation), and architectures (ensembles, transformers, detectors, GANs). However, their success depends on factors such as the availability and nature of data used for distillation, domain mismatch between teacher and student, robustness and privacy requirements, and optimization dynamics. KD can unlock high-performing compact models when combined with task-aware design choices (e.g., feature imitation, augmentations, architecture search, or ensemble teachers), but practitioners must account for trade-offs and failure modes to use it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted, practically driven set of techniques to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students for deep learning and NLP. KD operates at multiple levels — softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational maps, and structured layer mappings — and is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines that include pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data-aware strategies. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the provenance or synthesis of distillation data, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and out-of-distribution behaviors, and formal guarantees under constrained data or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. The literature frames KD as a multi-level toolkit—ranging from soft-target (logit) transfer to intermediate-feature and relational objectives—that is most effective when combined with task-aware data strategies and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data or domain mismatch, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible, task-aware toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, student pretraining), distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of a teacher’s utility. Realizing those gains in practice requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational structure), how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to source or synthesize distillation data under privacy or data-limited constraints, and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and domain-shift behavior. Responsible deployment therefore treats knowledge distillation as a core element of an integrated compression pipeline, with targeted interventions to mitigate capacity mismatch, teacher error transfer, and data- or distribution-driven failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default core technique for compressing large models into deployable students, because it provides a flexible set of transfer signals and composes naturally with other compression primitives. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success is conditional on careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches when necessary), and integration with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. A pragmatic pipeline view — choosing what to transfer, how to prepare students, and which auxiliary methods to include — yields the most reliable path to compact models that retain performance, robustness, and desirable properties in real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher in the form of softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has matured into a flexible toolkit that is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but success depends strongly on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data and optimization are handled. Remaining limitations include capacity and optimization mismatches, degradation on low-frequency or domain-specific behaviors, and risk of transferring teacher biases or vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for transferring useful behavior from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets and protocols—soft-target/logit matching, representation- and attention-level imitation, relational or correlation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data strategies that range from using original training data to augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols. KD is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that aligns student capacity and architecture with chosen signals and augments distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and degraded out-of-domain or long-tail behavior; addressing these requires targeted algorithmic, data, and evaluation advances.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, modality-agnostic approach to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as the default starting point for compression, KD provides multiple complementary signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) that—when matched to student capacity and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—produce strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is not universally sufficient: practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability and provenance, domain shift, teacher errors, and robustness/fairness constraints. A pragmatic compression pipeline therefore places KD at its center but integrates pretraining, architecture adaptation, data-aware distillation schedules, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal domains. The effectiveness of KD depends on careful, task‑aware design: selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures and capacities, choosing suitable data strategies, and mitigating propagated teacher errors or distributional shifts. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical techniques, empirical findings, limits, and recommendations distilled from recent literature.
