papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A broad toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations or attention maps, relational objectives, multi-teacher/online schedules, and data-centric strategies including data-free synthesis—enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success requires aligning distillation signals to student capacity, selecting appropriate data and augmentation strategies, combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), and explicitly addressing limits such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, distributional shift, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for converting large, high-performance deep models into smaller, deployable students. Responsible production use therefore treats KD as the core of a system-level compression pipeline—combined with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted evaluations for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific behavior—rather than as a standalone remedy.

Practical success depends on matching the distillation recipe to task needs, student capacity, and data constraints while explicitly managing teacher imperfections, distributional shift, and fairness or privacy concerns.

However, KD alone faces practical limits—data and domain mismatch, capacity gaps between teacher and student, and the need to preserve rare or safety-critical behaviors—so practitioners should treat KD as a central component of a compression toolkit rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, multi-signal strategy for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, and multi‑modal settings KD has expanded from matching softened output probabilities to a configurable toolbox that includes intermediate‑feature and attention alignment, relational/ensemble transfers, online and multi‑teacher schedules, and data‑side interventions such as augmentation or synthetic/example selection. In practice KD is most effective when treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that aligns student architecture and capacity, chooses appropriate distillation signals and data, and combines distillation with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, open problems remain in principled distillation under limited or private data, robustness to distribution shift and rare/event behaviors, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically proven approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a design‑sensitive pipeline element rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble knowledge and can be combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity and architecture, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and explicitly addressing robustness, fairness, and domain-shift failure modes. This paper argues KD should be the default core of compression workflows while highlighting necessary conditions, complementary techniques, and research directions to make distillation reliable in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, multi-faceted approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logits matching, distillation can be adapted to transfer inductive biases, deploy in federated or privacy-constrained settings, operate without access to original training data, and improve robustness and domain specialization. When combined with techniques such as feature mimicking, careful soft-label regularization, and online or ensemble-based training regimes, distillation provides a flexible toolkit to meet the efficiency, privacy, and deployment constraints of modern deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and production-oriented approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable, task-aware toolkit and combined with complementary techniques (pretraining of compact architectures, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis, and architecture-aware design), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, distillation signals and data regimes, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Responsible deployment requires targeted remedies for capacity mismatch, rare-token and distribution-shift failures, and propagation of teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure). Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logit matching to a toolkit that includes feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, multi- and reinforced multi-teacher strategies, data-free and augmentation-driven protocols, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architectures, and how to handle data availability and distributional shifts. Important limitations remain—propagation of teacher errors or biases, degraded rare- or out-of-domain behavior, and data- or privacy-constrained regimes—which motivate targeted algorithmic and data strategies to make distillation reliable in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Singh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Configurable Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact, deployable deep models. Treated as a configurable toolkit rather than a single algorithm, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teachers into smaller students and can be combined with complementary compression primitives, data strategies, and architecture co-design. When applied with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and downstream evaluation (including robustness and fairness), KD reliably yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and performance across tasks and modalities.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Practical Model Compression: A Conditional, Task‑Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default core of model compression for deep learning and NLP when the goal is to produce compact, deployable models that retain much of teacher performance. KD is versatile: it can transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure, and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data-side interventions. However, its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distillation signals, and the availability or synthesis of appropriate distillation data. To be reliable in production, KD must be applied as a configurable pipeline—combining multi-level objectives, student pretraining or architecture-aware projectors, complementary compression primitives, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Conditional, and Complementary for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations through softened outputs, feature- and relation-level objectives, and staged or multi-teacher schedules. As a default first-line technique it often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling substantial efficiency gains, but its success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives. Effective, production-ready compression pipelines therefore treat KD as the core engine embedded within a task-aware, data-conscious, and evaluation-driven workflow.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the System-Level Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and flexible paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students for deep learning and NLP. Treated as a system-level toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD supports multiple transfer objectives (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), composes with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), and enables deployment in data- or privacy-constrained scenarios. However, realizing those benefits in production requires careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and robustness degradation under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practical Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of training techniques that transfer information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving predictive performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, transferring relational structure among examples or channels, multi- and self-distillation, and data-aware protocols including data-free and domain-adaptive approaches. Its practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and task constraints, handling data availability and privacy, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques. While KD often yields deployable students that retain much of teacher utility, important limitations remain around domain shift, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and robustness to rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and structured-data domains. The core idea is to transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student via multiple possible signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure). In practice, KD is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that aligns teacher and student capacity, chooses distillation targets and data strategies to match deployment constraints, and pairs distillation with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Common failure modes include teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or heterogeneous data provenance, propagation of teacher errors and biases, and degraded robustness under distribution shift; these motivate practical remedies such as multi-teacher schemes, student pre-training, synthetic or data-free distillation, and targeted evaluation for robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can be combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (original, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and task-aware design choices. Open challenges include capacity mismatch, robustness under domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior, and operating without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, practical approach that compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behaviors, internal representations, or relational structure. Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that a tailored combination of distillation targets, architectural alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., quantization, pruning) yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints; however, success depends on careful design to avoid capacity mismatch, data or distributional mismatch, and unintended transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal, practical toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models in deep learning and NLP. KD methods range from softened-output matching to representation-level and relational transfers, and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices. KD routinely improves efficiency–performance trade-offs but has predictable limits—capacity mismatch, data and domain mismatch, and transfer of teacher errors or biases—that require explicit mitigation and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research has broadened KD from simple softened-logit matching to a toolbox that includes intermediate-feature alignment, relational or attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and staged training schedules, and data strategies ranging from augmentation to synthetic or data-free generation. When combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware adaptation, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Success hinges on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; remaining challenges include domain shift, capacity mismatch, low-frequency behavior in sequence tasks, and privacy-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical mechanism for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is most effective when treated as a configurable core of a broader compression pipeline: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and which complementary compression primitives to apply all materially affect outcomes. I argue that KD should be the default backbone of model-compression workflows in deep learning and NLP but must be embedded in design‑sensitive, hybrid pipelines that explicitly address capacity mismatch, data availability, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher (or ensemble) models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) while retaining most of the teacher’s utility. Across vision, speech, generative modeling, and NLP, practitioners use multiple KD signals (soft targets, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes) and combine KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware student design). Empirical practice and synthesis work show KD yields substantial efficiency gains when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data availability, and task constraints; remaining challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, reliable distillation without original data, and preserving robustness, fairness, and rare or low-frequency behaviors under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Success depends on choosing appropriate distillation strategies that account for model structure, task specificity, data availability, and training dynamics. When tailored—via structural transformations, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer alignment, or data-centric augmentations—distillation consistently produces compact models that approach teacher accuracy and enable real-world use cases that would otherwise be impractical.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers teacher behavior via softened outputs, intermediate-representation alignment, attention/relational signals, and ensemble-style targets. Its empirical success in reducing latency and memory while retaining much of teacher accuracy depends on student capacity, teacher preparation, data provenance (including synthetic or data‑free regimes), and integration with complementary primitives such as pruning, quantization, architecture design, and pretraining. Treating KD as a configurable, design‑sensitive component of a broader compression pipeline—rather than a single turnkey algorithm—yields the most reliable path to compact models that meet task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Pipeline Design, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most usefully viewed as a system-level, modular pipeline for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When KD combines soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, selective or synthesized data, multi-teacher aggregation, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery), it reliably yields small students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of transferred biases and domain shifts. Practical deployments therefore require principled choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and which data strategies to apply.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, multi-level approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information ranging from softened output distributions to intermediate representations and relational structure. Across vision and language applications, KD is typically integrated into broader compression pipelines that include pretraining of compact students, pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware redesign. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signals and data strategy to student capacity and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, and degraded robustness under distribution shift. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable, task-aware toolkit rather than a single recipe, combining appropriate transfer objectives, teacher–student alignment, and careful empirical evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has grown beyond soft-target matching to include representation-level and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, meta-learned teachers, and data-aware or data-free protocols. Combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD forms a practical core of modern compression pipelines. However, success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity and data availability, and on addressing failure modes like capacity mismatch, domain shift, and transfer of teacher biases. Emerging best practices emphasize pretraining compact students, careful selection or synthesis of distillation data, adaptive teacher strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods have become central tools for deploying large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Work in this area spans techniques that transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, approaches that operate without access to original training data, methods that preserve privacy or reduce communication in distributed settings, and specialized strategies for large pre-trained language and vision transformer models. Key themes include layer- and module-level mappings between teacher and student, task-aware selection of distilled signals, adversarial and generative approaches to synthesize training inputs, and the combination of pruning or architecture search with distillation. Practical trade-offs arise between fidelity to teacher behavior, student capacity, data availability, and robustness to distribution shifts or adversarial attacks. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous modalities and architectures, selecting what information to transfer for a given downstream task, and ensuring privacy and robustness while maintaining high compression ratios.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques reduce large, high-performing neural models to smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relationships. Methods vary from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate features, using multi-teacher ensembles, training students with surrogate or synthesized data when originals are unavailable, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map or align heterogeneous architectures, whether and how the student is pre-trained, and which data or augmentation strategies are used. While KD can recover much of a teacher's performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, open issues remain around robustness, distributional shifts, teacher imperfections, and principled optimization theory.

papers_seen.author: Cordova
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical—but Insufficient—Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD encompasses output-level soft-target transfer, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-side techniques including synthetic or data-free distillation. In practice, KD delivers large gains when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), task-aware data strategies, and explicit handling of teacher–student mismatches and distributional or safety-sensitive behaviors. A pragmatic position is that KD should serve as the central component of compression pipelines, but practitioners must adopt targeted adjunct methods and evaluation protocols to address capacity limitations, robustness, long-tail behavior, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescriptive Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in deep learning and NLP. When treated as a central toolkit—combining output-level supervision, representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware or data-free strategies, and integration with other compression primitives—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, or preservation of rare behaviors; realizing reliable compressed models requires deliberate teacher preparation, student-aware design, data or synthesis strategies, and explicit robustness and bias interventions.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-faceted, practical strategy for producing compact models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. Across many tasks and modalities, KD can transfer information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention patterns, relational structure) and is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture design, pruning, quantization, and appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic). Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling substantial gains in latency and deployability, but predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and challenges when original data are unavailable—require targeted mitigations. Practical recommendations center on matching distilled signals to student capacity and architecture, using projectors or layer mappings to align representations, combining KD with complementary compression primitives, and applying privacy-aware or data-free techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD techniques include matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate features or attention patterns, and using multi- or self-distillation schedules; they are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet deployment constraints. KD has been effective across vision, language, speech, and retrieval tasks, but its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student. Practical pipelines therefore choose distillation signals and data strategies that suit the target task, and complement KD with additional compression and validation to mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, and brittleness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs/logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure) and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free approaches). When designed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, signal selection, and data availability, KD routinely yields students that recover most of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, teacher bias propagation, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and distillation without original data, motivating targeted algorithmic and pipeline-level solutions.

papers_seen.author: Bradshaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners combine distillation objectives with complementary compression techniques and data strategies to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, obtaining or synthesizing suitable data for transfer, and validating robustness and fairness; important open problems remain around principled curricula, data-scarce distillation, and theoretical understanding of transfer mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible, task-aware toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, student pretraining), distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of a teacher’s utility. Realizing those gains in practice requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational structure), how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to source or synthesize distillation data under privacy or data-limited constraints, and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and domain-shift behavior. Responsible deployment therefore treats knowledge distillation as a core element of an integrated compression pipeline, with targeted interventions to mitigate capacity mismatch, teacher error transfer, and data- or distribution-driven failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so they meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Over the last decade KD has grown from soft-label (logit) matching into a practical toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free protocols. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when distillation choices are matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment requirements. At the same time, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, poor transfer of low-frequency behaviors, and sensitivity to distribution shift—so robust deployment requires task-aware design, careful data strategies, representation-aware objectives, and thorough evaluation across distributions and metrics beyond accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical route to compressing large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students for deep learning and NLP. Treated as a configurable toolkit rather than a single algorithm, KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure) and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD routinely produces strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs when teacher signals, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen to match deployment constraints; however, predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, limited or private data, propagation of teacher errors, and degraded long‑tail or fairness properties—require targeted adaptations, principled evaluation, and hybrid pipelines to obtain robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When framed as a composable pipeline—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning architectures, managing or synthesizing distillation data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain-shifted inputs. Best practice treats KD as one essential component of a broader, task-aware compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and a Design-Sensitive Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, highly practical approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and architecture search. Its consistent empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a default technique for many deployment pipelines. However, KD is not automatic: reliable compression requires careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, how distillation data are chosen or synthesized, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and domain-shift risks. A pragmatic, system-level KD workflow combines pretraining of compact architectures, targeted distillation objectives, complementary compression primitives, and evaluation focused on rare and out-of-domain behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, system-level toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques transfer information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure; they can be combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies that include augmentation, synthetic generation, or data-free approaches. Effective distillation depends on matching the distillation signals, student architecture, and data strategy to task and deployment constraints. While well-designed KD pipelines often recover most teacher performance, remaining challenges include optimization instability, transfer of teacher errors or biases, handling limited or private data, and preserving rare-token/long-tail behavior in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A range of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and procedural variants—multi-teacher schedules, online/self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware pipelines—enable deployment of compact models across vision and NLP while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success hinges on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, choosing appropriate training data or synthesis strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). KD also has well-documented failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, distribution shift) that require tailored remedies. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative applications, practical recommendations, and open challenges for using KD as an integrated compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a practical, multimodal toolkit that reliably shrinks large models into deployable students while preserving much of their utility. When treated as the central component of compression pipelines and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD delivers substantial gains in latency, memory, and communication efficiency. However, safe and effective use of KD requires careful, task-aware choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle data scarcity or privacy limits, and how to combine distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or student pretraining. This paper argues KD should be the default engine for model compression in deep learning and NLP, outlines its key mechanisms, highlights practical limitations and failure modes, and provides concrete recommendations for robust, deployed KD pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multi-signal toolkit that routinely enables deployment of large models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure into smaller students. When integrated into a pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, complementary compression (pruning, quantization), and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized), KD often recovers most teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success is conditional on careful choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors; open challenges remain in data-free distillation and in preventing propagation of teacher errors and biases.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, and relational structure. Over the past decade KD has diversified from simple soft-target matching into a configurable toolkit that includes logits/soft-label transfer, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free protocols. In practice, KD is most effective when embedded in a task-aware compression pipeline that aligns teacher signals, student capacity, and data strategies, and that combines distillation with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Key limitations include capacity mismatch, domain and data-shift sensitivity, propagation of teacher weaknesses (biases or calibration errors), and challenges preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors; these motivate targeted interventions such as layer-aware objectives, channel- or attention-focused transfers, teacher selection or weighting, and careful evaluation for robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Methods span matching softened output distributions, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive module replacement, channel- and module-aware transfers, and data-free or generative approaches for when original training data are unavailable. Practical pipelines combine KD with quantization, low-precision training, pruning, or architecture transformations and often rely on staged or adaptive teacher-student schedules. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and NLP tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, what and which samples are distilled, data availability, and careful engineering of interfaces between heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Burgess
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring information from large "teacher" models into smaller "student" models so that compact models approach the performance of their teachers while reducing inference cost and memory footprint. KD methods range from matching softened output logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational structures; they can operate with single or multiple teachers, with or without original training data, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical work shows KD reliably improves deployment efficiency across classification, generation, detection, and retrieval tasks, but practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing suitable data or synthesis strategies, and mitigating limits including capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, domain shift, and concerns about robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure. It is a flexible toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, enable low-precision inference, and support privacy- and data-constrained settings. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity and task, choosing appropriate data or synthetic surrogates when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Key open problems include capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and principled design of teacher–student schedules.

KD should therefore be treated as the central element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity and architecture, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and explicitly addressing robustness, fairness, and domain-shift failure modes. This paper argues KD should be the default core of compression workflows while highlighting necessary conditions, complementary techniques, and research directions to make distillation reliable in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. Research spans theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps, practical methods for compressing pretrained language models, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, strategies to preserve robustness, and distributed/federated adaptations. Methods include soft-label matching, intermediate feature/attention imitation, many-to-many layer mappings, task-adaptive architecture search, and self-distillation. Empirical and theoretical work highlights gains in efficiency and deployment feasibility across vision and NLP tasks, while also revealing limitations related to data distribution, teacher quality, robustness, and low-frequency token coverage. Open directions include principled handling of imperfect teachers, domain adaptation during compression, robustness-aware distillation, and scalable distillation in distributed or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and a Task-Aware Workflow
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an integrated, task-aware pipeline and combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher utility. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on student capacity, what is transferred (logits, features, relations), data availability, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and domain-shift risks. I argue KD should be the central engine of model compression pipelines while practitioners explicitly address its known failure modes through design choices and validation.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transforms large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring behavioral and representational information. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines, often combined with pre-training and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), produce compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting application-specific requirements. However, effective distillation depends on student capacity, data or synthetic-data strategies, teacher quality, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift; these limitations motivate hybrid pipelines and careful evaluation.

Practical pipelines therefore treat distillation as an integrated system component, selecting transfer signals and data procedures that match deployment constraints and validating for fairness, privacy, and robustness.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically driven set of techniques that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to achieve reductions in latency, memory, and computational cost while preserving much of task performance. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts as a regularizer that helps students approach teacher accuracy, but its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and careful engineering to avoid propagating teacher errors or losing robustness. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a configurable system combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and domain-aware data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, modular technique in modern model-compression pipelines: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller students while remaining flexible enough to combine with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-side interventions. KD’s practical success depends on deliberate choices—what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to evaluate robustness and long-tail behavior. When used as part of a system that addresses optimization, data, and mismatch issues, KD frequently yields compact models that meet deployment constraints; when used alone or carelessly it can underperform or propagate undesirable behaviors. The remainder of this paper argues for KD as the default, central component of compression toolkits while outlining its limits and concrete design recommendations to mitigate them.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool That Requires Integrated, Task-Aware Pipelines for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and widely applicable technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. While KD supplies a flexible set of signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention, and relational structure) that often preserves much of a teacher's performance, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and careful evaluation. KD alone does not guarantee robustness to distribution shift, immunity to propagated teacher biases, or preservation of rare-event behavior; achieving reliable deployment therefore requires integrated, task-aware workflows including pretraining, selective or confidence-weighted transfer, feature-mimicking choices, and architecture- or data-level interventions.

papers_seen.author: Barr
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a configurable, multi-signal component of practical compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD can enable compact models that retain much of a teacher’s utility. Realizing that potential requires combining logits- and representation-level signals, integrating complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), handling limited or private data, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be adopted as the default, pipeline-aware approach to compression while research focuses on principled teacher selection, automated signal scheduling, and robustness-aware distillation.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to improve efficiency while retaining performance. Methods span logits-based soft-label transfer, feature- or layer-wise matching, adversarial and data-free distillation, architecture-aware projection or search, and task-adaptive compression for NLP. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision, speech, generative models, and language models; recent theory clarifies when and why soft labels help and when mixing hard labels matters. Practical designs—attention-guided layer alignment, projectors or ensembles of projectors, and careful data augmentation or synthetic-data generation—substantially affect student quality. Open challenges include data-privacy constraints, distillation across heterogeneous architectures, preserving teacher errors, and better theoretical/empirical guidance for designing KD pipelines for diverse tasks.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Hybrid Tool for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple transfer signals and schedules that can recover much of a teacher’s performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. However, distillation is not sufficient on its own: combining KD with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), pretraining or adapting the student, and applying data-aware strategies improves robustness, domain transfer, and preservation of rare behaviors. A pragmatic, task-aware pipeline—choosing appropriate signals to transfer, preparing student models, augmenting or synthesizing data, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness—yields the most reliable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs for production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi‑signal approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models from larger teachers. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened teacher outputs to a broad toolbox that includes intermediate representation and attention matching, relational objectives, multi‑ and self‑distillation, and data‑side interventions (including synthetic and data‑free methods). KD is most effective when integrated into an end‑to‑end compression pipeline—paired with architecture design, pruning, quantization, or dataset strategies—and when the distillation recipe (signals, schedule, and data) is matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Despite frequent empirical success in preserving much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, KD has well‑documented limits: capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, sensitivity to data availability and distribution shift, and challenges in preserving rare‑class or long‑tail behaviors. Practical deployment therefore requires task‑aware design, explicit robustness and fairness evaluation, and often a combination of KD with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mcdaniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Task‑Aware Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller students so they can meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a task‑aware, design‑sensitive toolkit and combined with complementary compression methods (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies), KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher utility. KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits depend on signal selection, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. Practical success follows from choosing what to transfer, how to align layers and architectures, and how to prepare or synthesize data and training schedules to mitigate predictable failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure, and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization) and with data- or curriculum-driven strategies. Across vision, language, generative models, and policy settings, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory; however, it has clear limits related to capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data availability, and optimization instability. Real-world deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable engineering toolkit rather than a single recipe, combining careful choice of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. A family of methods—matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and synthesizing or selecting data—enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Success in real systems depends on task-aware design, careful teacher–student pairing, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. It is a practical toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, to adapt models across domains, and to support privacy-aware or federated settings. Empirical work across vision, speech, graphs, and language tasks shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers are configured, and how training is regularized materially affect the trade-offs between efficiency and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Not Sufficient Tool for Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial runtime, memory, and latency gains while preserving much of predictive performance. KD is effective across modalities and deployment regimes, but its success depends on careful method choice, teacher quality, data availability, and combination with complementary compression strategies. Future progress requires deeper theoretical understanding, better automation for heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive settings, and principled integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.
