papers_seen.author: Valentine
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-label matching into multi-level pipelines that include logits transfer, feature and attention imitation, relational losses, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-constrained variants (data-free, few-shot, privacy-aware). Empirical work shows KD frequently yields deployable models that retain much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution examples, principled sample selection, and formal guarantees under limited data or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Hampton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Central but Insufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed with attention to what signals are transferred, student capacity, and the provenance of distillation data, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD alone does not guarantee reliable deployment: practical pipelines must combine distillation with architecture-aware design, representation-level alignment, complementary compression methods, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior. A task-aware, multi-stage pipeline—incorporating teacher adaptation, student pretraining, data strategies (including data-free approaches when necessary), and pruning/quantization—produces the most dependable compressed models for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Meza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Approaches include matching softened teacher logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational structure, and exploiting multi-teacher or online schemes. KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search and can be adapted for low-data or data-free settings. Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines often recover much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures and capacities, how to manage or synthesize data, and how to mitigate robustness and fairness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible engineering toolkit that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students. When designed as the core of an integrated compression pipeline and matched to task constraints—choice of distilled signals, student capacity and architecture, data regimen and augmentation, and complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. However, KD is not a universal cure: its benefits depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful engineering to avoid transferring teacher errors, degrading robustness, or worsening fairness. Practitioners should therefore adopt KD as a default starting point for compression but implement task‑aware recipes, layer- or projector-aware mappings, data strategies, and pipeline-level safeguards to produce reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across vision and NLP, effective distillation combines choices about what to transfer (soft outputs, features, relational signals), how teachers are designed or ensembled, and what data or surrogates are used. Practical pipelines increasingly pair distillation with architecture search, curriculum strategies, and distributed training to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often recovers much of a teacher's performance, success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data complexity, and optimization procedures; open problems include principled handling of imperfect teachers, robustness and fairness under compression, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a configurable system rather than a single recipe. By choosing which teacher signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student architectures, and applying task- and data-aware strategies (including multi-teacher aggregation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and architecture search), practitioners can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD delivers practical gains across vision and NLP but requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors, mismatching capacities, or degrading robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Kramer
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods extend beyond matching teacher output probabilities to include intermediate-representation and relational transfers, multi- and self-distillation, and protocols that operate with limited or synthesized data. In practice KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines that consider student architecture, complementary primitives (pruning, quantization), and data strategies. Despite strong empirical benefits, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity and optimization mismatch, degradation on low-frequency or domain-specific behaviors, and transfer of teacher biases or vulnerabilities—which motivate continued work on alignment methods, data-free distillation, and robustness-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Tool Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible family of methods that, when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression techniques, enables deployment of compact models with strong utility. KD can transfer final-output behavior, intermediate representations, and structured relationships; it can operate with or without original training data, be adapted for privacy-sensitive or federated settings, and be combined with quantization or pruning to meet hardware constraints. Effective practice requires attention to what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how KD is integrated into the broader compression pipeline to avoid propagation of teacher biases or degradation on rare or shifted data.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device or latency-constrained deployment when its signals, data strategy, and architecture alignment are chosen to match task and deployment constraints, but it has well-documented limitations related to teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modular approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-target matching to a versatile toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data-side strategies (including synthetic and privacy-aware approaches). When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful teacher–student alignment, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance; however, its effectiveness is conditional on student capacity, data provenance, teacher quality, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of KD variants and complementary compression techniques enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and data-availability constraints. Empirical work shows KD frequently recovers much of teacher performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints; however, practical pipelines must manage trade-offs and persistent gaps in robustness, domain-shift handling, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Camacho
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. A spectrum of techniques—from softened-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive or relational objectives, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches—has been developed and validated across vision, language, graph, and speech tasks. Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, preparing the student (including pretraining or student-aware teacher design), selecting or synthesizing distillation data, and composing KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Key limitations include capacity and optimization mismatch, domain- and data-shift, preservation of rare-token or long-tail behavior in NLP, and robustness or fairness transfer; addressing these requires task-aware distillation recipes and integrated pipelines that balance compactness, accuracy, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Berg
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal, practically oriented approach for making large neural models deployable by training smaller students to capture a teacher’s predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond soft-target matching to include intermediate-representation and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware protocols (including synthetic and data-free approaches). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when distillation choices are matched to student capacity, data provenance, and deployment constraints. Persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors or biases, degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena, principled sample selection under limited data, and providing formal guarantees for robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Conditional
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals) and is most effective when integrated with complementary practices such as pre-training, architecture-aware design, data-side strategies, and other compression techniques. However, its success is conditional on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or mismatched data, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher errors or biases. Treating KD as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe yields the best results for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Task-Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective engine for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. KD’s flexibility—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-teacher schedules, and operating with or without original data—makes it the practical backbone of compression pipelines. However, distillation can amplify teacher biases, struggle with rare-token or long-tail behavior, and depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; practitioners should therefore adopt integrated, task-aware KD workflows combined with complementary compression techniques and explicit evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Porter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Practically useful KD workflows combine multiple distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational objectives), data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized), and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware student design). Empirical work shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across NLP and other modalities, but its success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, and explicit treatment of robustness, fairness, and privacy; open problems include preserving rare-token behaviors, domain shift, and communication- or data-constrained distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Workflows, and Limitations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, speech, and natural language tasks. KD unifies a variety of objectives—soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational losses, and multi-teacher or self-distillation—often combined with data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free) and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). When applied as an integrated, task-aware pipeline, KD frequently yields compact models that preserve most of a teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, benefits are conditional: student capacity, data availability or mismatch, architectural heterogeneity, and potential transfer of teacher errors or undesirable behaviors require careful signal selection, tailored data protocols, and targeted evaluation to ensure robust, fair, and reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods such as quantization or architecture search—distillation can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities. However, KD has limits: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity or absence, and optimization subtleties can reduce gains. Practical deployment therefore benefits from hybrid pipelines that adapt KD objectives to task constraints, incorporate robustness and privacy considerations, and use auxiliary compression techniques where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Reynolds
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses functionality from larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. A diverse set of KD variants — softened-logit matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data‑free or privacy-aware protocols — has enabled substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when training pipelines address teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints. Persistent challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors (important in NLP), robustness and fairness under distillation, and producing reliable distilled models when original training data are limited or private.

papers_seen.author: York
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted paradigm for producing compact, deployable models from large teacher networks. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal structure using a variety of signals and schedules, and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design. Empirical work shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, and graph settings, but its success depends on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher quality, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-case behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesized Evidence and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. A broad family of KD objectives and protocols—soft-target matching, feature and attention mimicry, relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes—has been developed and empirically validated across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD is most effective when treated as a system that aligns teacher and student capacity, chooses what signals to transfer, and composes with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or low-precision numerics). Successful deployment depends on data strategies (real-data distillation, augmentation, or synthetic/data-free methods), student initialization or pretraining, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy constraints. Remaining research directions include principled layer mapping for large pre-trained models, reliable distillation without original data, preserving robustness and rare-event behaviors, and theoretical understanding of optimization dynamics under capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Responses
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural signals. Across vision and NLP, KD variants—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi- and self-teaching, and combinations with pruning/quantization—enable reduced inference cost and on-device deployment while attempting to retain performance. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD acts both as a route to transfer representational inductive biases and as a form of learned regularization; its success depends on signal choice, data provenance, capacity mismatch, and optimization. Methodological refinements (data augmentation, adversarial or boundary-focused examples, data-free synthesis, teacher design, and divergence choices) address core challenges in practice, but open problems remain around robustness, privacy, fairness, and reliably closing the teacher–student performance gap.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at the level of outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows distilled students can often recover much of a teacher's performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, the teacher–student capacity relationship, data availability, and optimization strategy. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs distillation signals with student preparation, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression methods to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Hammond
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Composable, but Conditional Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. KD provides multiple transferable signals — softened outputs, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, and relational or ensemble objectives — and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-side interventions. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs, reliable deployment requires design choices that match distilled signals to student capacity, appropriate handling or synthesis of distillation data, and explicit mitigation of predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, and degraded long-tail or out-of-distribution behavior. Treated as the core of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline and combined with complementary compression primitives and careful evaluation, KD is the most practical route to compact models that approach teacher utility in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and NLP. KD operates across levels—from softened outputs to intermediate representations, attention or relational structure—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized). Empirical and practitioner literature shows KD can recover much of teacher performance under realistic deployment constraints, but success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns. A task-aware, multi-stage KD pipeline that pairs representation-level transfer with architecture-aware pretraining and selective complementary compression yields the most reliable trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Williamson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central but Insufficient — A Task‑Aware, Integrated Approach for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable mechanism for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD encompasses many signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure) and operates across regimes from data-rich to data-free. Its strengths make it an ideal backbone for compression pipelines, but its effectiveness is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, and robustness and fairness constraints. Consequently, KD should be treated as the central component of an integrated, task-aware compression workflow that explicitly combines signal selection, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to mitigate predictable failure modes and meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wallace
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods range from matching teacher soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure; they can operate with or without original training data and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and architecture search. Successful use of KD in practice requires careful design choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities and architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to evaluate and mitigate failure modes such as degraded low-frequency token behavior, propagation of teacher biases, and domain-shift fragility.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal signals from large teacher models into smaller student models so they meet real-world deployment constraints. KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when its objectives, data, and architecture mapping are chosen deliberately. However, KD is not sufficient on its own: capacity mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, and the risk of propagating teacher errors mean KD must be embedded in hybrid pipelines that include complementary compression methods, targeted data strategies, and explicit robustness and fairness evaluations.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, and structural signals. A broad family of distillation techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and attention-level alignment, relational objectives, multi-stage and multi-teacher schemes, and data- or generator-based approaches—supports large reductions in parameter count and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when integrated with task-aware student design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Important limitations include capacity mismatch, optimization instability, propagation of teacher errors, and challenges in low-data or privacy-constrained regimes; addressing these requires careful selection of what to transfer, how to align teachers and students, and when to employ auxiliary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has diversified from matching softened teacher outputs into a toolkit that also transfers intermediate features, attention and relational structure, and that can operate with real, augmented, or synthesized data. In practice KD is usually combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tuned for deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, privacy). Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear benefits (improved sample efficiency, regularization, domain adaptation, enabling on-device use) alongside systematic limitations (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, optimization difficulties, and challenges under data scarcity), motivating hybrid, task-aware pipelines and ongoing research into robust data-free methods, principled teacher selection, and fairness/robustness preservation.

papers_seen.author: Reynolds
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a versatile, practically oriented pathway to compress large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated into a pipeline that includes student pretraining, targeted selection of distilled signals, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression primitives, KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s benefits are conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and distributional shift impose predictable limits that require explicit mitigation and evaluation. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware system — not a one-size-fits-all recipe — yields the best trade-offs for production deployment.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing models to smaller, efficient models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature has diversified beyond simple teacher→student logit-matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, online and federated protocols, teacher-free and data-free variants, and architectural co-design. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D perception, and NLP demonstrates that carefully chosen distillation signals, layer mappings, and training practices (e.g., pretraining, projected feature matching, selective sample weighting) produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance; remaining challenges include data heterogeneity, privacy, robustness, and automating teacher–student pairing and signal selection.

Empirical evidence shows that, when KD is treated as a system—matching distillation signals to student capacity, aligning inputs and architectures, and using complementary compression primitives—students often recover much of teacher performance while delivering large efficiency gains. Important open problems remain in robustness, fairness, low-frequency or long‑tail behavior, reliable distillation without original data, and principled curricula for multi-source transfer.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation enables deployment of powerful pretrained models in resource-constrained settings, supports specialization (e.g., task or domain adaptation), and can be combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search) to produce practical, production-ready models. Advances in distillation methodology — including multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, teacher meta-learning, and task-aware layer-wise alignment — address fundamental challenges of capacity mismatch, information selection, and optimization stability, leading to more robust and efficient student models. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of any production-focused compression pipeline for deep learning and NLP systems, and that research emphasis on better teacher–student dynamics and task-aware transfer will yield the largest practical gains.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while aiming to preserve task performance. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a diverse set of techniques that supervise logits, internal representations, attention maps, and relational structures, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data strategies. Despite widespread practical success across vision and language tasks, KD’s effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability and provenance, and training dynamics; open problems include reliably preserving rare behaviors, automating signal selection, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used technique to transfer information from larger or more complex models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models. It serves both model compression and training-stabilization roles across vision, speech, and language tasks. KD variants include offline teacher-student distillation, online/co-distillation among peers, feature- and representation-level matching, and hybrid schemes that combine distillation with quantization or specialized training objectives. Empirical evidence shows KD can improve accuracy, generalization, robustness, and inference efficiency, but its success depends on data complexity, teacher design, and the type of knowledge transferred.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment constraints. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, appropriate data strategies, and careful teacher–student design. While KD frequently yields compact models that retain most teacher performance and can improve robustness or enable low-precision inference, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—making KD a powerful but context-sensitive tool rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a broad toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distilled students often recover much of a teacher's performance when teacher–student capacity, distilled signals, and data strategies are chosen carefully, but persistent failure modes (capacity mismatch, teacher error transfer, domain shift, and degraded low-frequency behavior) require targeted remedies. Practical use treats KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs appropriate distillation signals with student preparation, data curation or synthesis, and complementary compression techniques to produce compact, robust models suitable for resource- and privacy-constrained deployment.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the default core technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure when its signals, data, and optimization are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD must be applied as a system-level, design-sensitive pipeline—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, privacy-aware procedures, and complementary compression primitives—to avoid optimization failures, capacity mismatch, and propagation of teacher errors. I recommend KD-first workflows that explicitly plan for data, evaluation under shift, and targeted mitigations for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring behavior from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable practical deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. The field has expanded beyond matching softened logits to include layer- and feature-level supervision, relational or contrastive signals, online and multi-teacher schemes, and methods that operate with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical work shows that when distillation recipes are matched to student capacity, architecture, and data availability, students can recover a large fraction of teacher performance; remaining challenges include propagation of teacher errors (especially for low-frequency phenomena), robustness under distributional shift, principled teacher selection, and distillation in data- or privacy-constrained regimes. Combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, progressive replacement) and task-aware design typically improves outcomes.
