papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be the default starting point for practical model-compression workflows in deep learning and NLP because it provides a flexible, multi-signal mechanism to transfer behavior from large teachers into compact students. Its strengths—ability to match softened outputs, align intermediate representations, and integrate with data-side strategies—make KD well suited to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success is conditional on careful choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-event behavior. A production-ready approach treats KD as the core of a task-aware, multi-stage pipeline that combines architecture-aware student design, complementary compression primitives, data strategies, and focused diagnostics to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Component of Practical Model-Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a modular element of a compression pipeline—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives such as pruning or quantization—KD routinely yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs. Its reliability depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, and how to handle data, privacy, and distributional concerns. KD should therefore be the default tool in compression workflows but applied with explicit mitigations for its known limits (capacity mismatch, teacher artifacts, rare-token behaviors, and robustness under shift).

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, system-level approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to compact students. The KD toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free protocols. In practice KD is often combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture surgery) and student pretraining or domain adaptation to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on task-aware design choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to supply distillation data, and how to monitor transferred errors or biases—and remains conditioned by data availability, teacher quality, and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Necessarily Integrated into a Broader Compression Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for converting large, high-performance deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers substantial parameter and latency savings while preserving much of teacher performance, but its reliability depends on engineering choices about what to transfer, how to prepare teachers and students, data provenance and augmentation, and complementary compression methods. Responsible production use therefore treats KD as the core of a system-level compression pipeline—combined with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted evaluations for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific behavior—rather than as a standalone remedy.

papers_seen.author: Craig
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened teacher logits to a flexible, multi-signal engineering toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Practical KD transfers information at multiple levels (outputs, intermediate features, attention/relations), is combined with data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free methods) and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), and is most effective when integrated as a task- and capacity-aware component of an end-to-end compression pipeline. Success is conditional on careful choice of distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagated teacher errors, domain shift, and privacy or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default core technique for compressing large models into deployable students, because it provides a flexible set of transfer signals and composes naturally with other compression primitives. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success is conditional on careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches when necessary), and integration with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. A pragmatic pipeline view — choosing what to transfer, how to prepare students, and which auxiliary methods to include — yields the most reliable path to compact models that retain performance, robustness, and desirable properties in real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for producing compact, deployable neural models by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD encompasses a spectrum of objectives — from matching soft output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, relational statistics, or task-specific features — and it is often combined with architectural modification, pruning, quantization, or data synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Practical KD addresses data scarcity, domain shift, heterogeneity of devices and architectures, and privacy concerns through strategies such as data-free distillation, multi-teacher weighting, teacher adaptation, and curriculum or instance-aware sampling. While KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, careful design is needed to avoid capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degradation on rare or out-of-domain inputs.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints by trading modest amounts of accuracy for substantial reductions in compute and footprint. When treated as an engineering toolkit—combining output-level supervision, intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data-aware strategies—KD reliably produces compact models that meet real-world constraints; success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity and attention to optimization, data selection, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Spence
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. The approach spans matching teacher outputs, imitating intermediate representations, distilling relational structure, and combining distillation with architecture- and data-side interventions. KD is widely used to reduce inference cost and memory footprint, enable on-device and privacy-aware deployment, and adapt models across domains; its success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and mitigation of bias and robustness trade-offs. Practical pipelines treat KD as a central, composable element combined with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and task-aware data strategies to produce compact models that approach teacher performance under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple transfer mechanisms (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals) and is most effective when integrated into a larger compression pipeline that includes data strategies, student-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance, but predictable limits (student capacity mismatch, data or privacy constraints, teacher errors and biases, and domain-shift fragility) require careful engineering and evaluation for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows that appropriately chosen distillation targets, careful teacher–student alignment, and combination with complementary compression techniques can produce compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Success depends on design choices—what signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, data provenance and augmentation, and mitigation of teacher errors or bias—so effective distillation is a pragmatic engineering pipeline rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Rose
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically driven paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. In practice KD functions as a configurable toolkit: practitioners choose which teacher signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention, relational structure), how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, and how to source or synthesize data for distillation. KD has enabled substantial reductions in model size and latency across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks (including pretrained Transformer models), but its success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and attention to robustness, privacy, and distributional shift. Practical pipelines therefore combine KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and targeted procedures (multi-teacher aggregation, student-friendly teacher training, data augmentation, or data-free distillation) to close the gap to teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Compression with Complementary Needs and Clear Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful engineering toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. In practice KD often delivers large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, but its success depends on task- and data-aware design: what signals are transferred, how teacher and student architectures are aligned, and how data scarcity, domain shift, privacy, and fairness concerns are handled. I argue KD should be the default starting point for compression pipelines, applied with explicit attention to complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware mapping), data strategies (data-free approaches or targeted synthesis), and safeguards against capacity mismatch and propagated biases.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Remaining Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven, flexible strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling large reductions in parameters and latency, and it generalizes across settings from data-poor or privacy-sensitive deployments to multi-teacher and online training regimes. However, practical success depends on careful choice of what to transfer (logits, features, relations), handling limited or absent training data, mitigating transferred biases, and aligning teacher-student architectures. I argue that KD should be the primary tool in production compression pipelines but must be combined with data synthesis, teacher selection/calibration, and fairness-aware design to realize robust, reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing deep models for real-world deployment. KD unifies multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational/attention matching) and interoperates naturally with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data synthesis). Properly designed KD pipelines—choosing what to transfer, mapping teacher and student representations, and addressing data or privacy constraints—yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across classification, generation, detection, and language tasks. At the same time, KD has limits (capacity mismatch, optimization and data mismatch, and potential propagation of teacher biases), so production pipelines must combine KD with pretraining, data strategies, and robustness/fairness checks to be reliable.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. A broad repertoire of KD techniques transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate-feature or attention matching, and relational or layer-wise alignment, and these techniques are commonly combined with data augmentation, teacher schedules, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distributional match, and optimization protocols. Best practice treats KD as a flexible toolkit to be adapted to deployment constraints rather than a single fixed recipe; key open challenges include theoretical understanding, robust distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and preserving fairness and rare-behavior fidelity during compression.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a broad toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distilled students often recover much of a teacher's performance when teacher–student capacity, distilled signals, and data strategies are chosen carefully, but persistent failure modes (capacity mismatch, teacher error transfer, domain shift, and degraded low-frequency behavior) require targeted remedies. Practical use treats KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs appropriate distillation signals with student preparation, data curation or synthesis, and complementary compression techniques to produce compact, robust models suitable for resource- and privacy-constrained deployment.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD techniques include matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate features or attention patterns, and using multi- or self-distillation schedules; they are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet deployment constraints. KD has been effective across vision, language, speech, and retrieval tasks, but its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student. Practical pipelines therefore choose distillation signals and data strategies that suit the target task, and complement KD with additional compression and validation to mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, and brittleness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Contemporary Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level approach for producing compact deep and NLP models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD techniques range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations and relational structures. When integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and data-aware training practices, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and provenance, and careful optimization; accordingly, KD is best treated as a central, composable element of a broader compression toolkit rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses the functionality of larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and NLP, KD variants—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, online and multi-teacher schemes, and task-adaptive architecture search—have enabled deployment of compact models with strong empirical performance while revealing trade-offs in teacher–student alignment, data availability, and robustness. Key open challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, effective data-free distillation, and preserving fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors during compression.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a multifaceted technique that both compresses large models for efficient deployment and provides regularizing, transfer, and adaptation benefits beyond simple model-size reduction. KD can be integrated with architectural compression, multi-teacher training, and modality transfer to produce compact models that retain or even improve task performance while enabling deployment on heterogeneous devices and privacy-sensitive settings. However, KD is not a silver bullet: teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and distilled-data artifacts can harm downstream behavior, so careful protocol design (multi-teacher aggregation, mixing hard labels, data-aware schemes, or data-free metadata approaches) and attention to internal-representation alignment are necessary to realize KD’s full potential.

papers_seen.author: Ewing
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal, pipeline-oriented approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, progressive or module-replacement schedules, and multi- or self-distillation schemes. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with deliberate data strategies (original-data augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols). Its empirical strengths are conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, alignment of signals to architecture, and robust evaluation for distribution shift, fairness, and privacy. Emerging work addresses data-free distillation and progressive module-replacing strategies, while open problems remain around principled objective selection, preserving rare-case behavior, and automation of architecture-agnostic pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students by transferring learned behavior or representations. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational information and are often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on what signals are transferred, student capacity and initialization, data strategies during distillation, and addressing robustness, privacy, and distributional mismatch. While distilled students frequently approach teacher performance, open problems remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preventing transfer of teacher errors or biases, and designing data-efficient or privacy-preserving distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques reduce the size and runtime of large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teacher models to a smaller student model. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, methods vary in what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, relations, or latent experts), how training data are used (original data, distilled predictions, or no data), and how multiple or imperfect teachers are combined. Practical adaptations include task-specific losses, sample selection or weighting, and architectural transformations; KD is also integrated with system-level strategies such as federated learning and pruning to meet device constraints. Empirical results show KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing compute and memory, but success depends on choices of teacher strength, data availability, multi-teacher aggregation, and whether task structure (e.g., localization or ranking) is explicitly addressed.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or constrained students. Techniques span matching teacher outputs (soft labels), aligning intermediate representations, layer-wise mappings, and data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthesized data, or data-free protocols). Effective deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and training choices (pretraining, curriculum schedules, ensemble-to-single transfers). Despite broad empirical success across vision, language, retrieval, and generative tasks, KD requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability, and optimization dynamics to realize robust, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Gregory
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Design-Sensitive Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central component of modern model-compression pipelines: a flexible, multi-signal toolkit that reliably transfers a large portion of teacher performance to smaller, deployable students when it is applied with deliberate, task-aware design. KD excels at trading accuracy for latency and memory across vision and language settings but is not a panacea; its safe and effective use requires matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and curricula, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods and targeted interventions for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention patterns—and often yields substantial improvements in latency, memory, and deployability relative to naive student training. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and privacy constraints, and whether complementary compression methods are applied. Viewed as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables flexible, task-aware compression pipelines that can be adapted to real-world constraints while acknowledging remaining limits around robustness, data-free operation, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD is effective across modalities and tasks, from question answering and speech recognition to vision and federated learning, but its success depends on careful handling of teacher imperfections, data artifacts, and deployment constraints. Best practices include using multi-teacher or staged distillation, blending soft and hard targets, engineering teacher-student interfaces (e.g., projectors or student-aware teachers), and combining KD with complementary techniques such as quantization or federated momentum. When these strategies are applied thoughtfully, KD enables high-quality compact models suitable for real-world, resource-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behaviors and internal signals. A broad family of KD methods—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, and data- or task-aware variants—has been applied across vision and language tasks. Practical deployment typically combines KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires attention to data availability, teacher–student alignment, and robustness or fairness concerns. Open challenges include principled handling of teacher errors, data-free distillation, and reliable transfer of robustness and fairness properties.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Central, Task-Aware, and Bounded Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically driven toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure, and they are most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful data choices, and student-aware design. KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance for many applications, but its success is not automatic: capacity mismatch, limited or private data, propagation of teacher errors, and degraded behaviour on long-tail or fairness-sensitive cases are persistent concerns. Thus KD should be treated as the practical core of compression pipelines when deployed with principled, task-aware adaptations and rigorous evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, multi-signal toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance when its signals, data, and teacher–student design are carefully chosen and when it is integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). At the same time, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: student capacity, data availability or provenance, teacher quality, and robustness/fairness concerns all shape outcomes. This synthesis summarizes what is known about KD’s methods, mechanisms, practical benefits, and remaining challenges, and outlines recommended pipeline principles for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Griffith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Conditional for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. It transfers teacher behavior through multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational structure), and when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware engineering it often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on student capacity and architecture alignment, the provenance and sufficiency of distillation data, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behaviors. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a configurable component and pairs it with targeted interventions (data strategies, architecture-aware transforms, and evaluation under deployment conditions) to achieve reliable efficiency–performance trade‑offs.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Aware Tool for Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single compression trick: when applied thoughtfully it enables deployment of large models by producing smaller, faster students while preserving task performance and transferring useful inductive biases. KD variants—matching outputs, aligning internal representations, using multi-teacher or data-free schemes, and pairing with augmentation or architecture-aware design—address diverse deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift). KD has demonstrable benefits but also concrete failure modes (teacher errors, data mismatch, capacity gaps) that require methodical mitigation and integration with complementary techniques such as pretraining, pruning, or data synthesis.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Methods span matching softened output distributions, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive module replacement, channel- and module-aware transfers, and data-free or generative approaches for when original training data are unavailable. Practical pipelines combine KD with quantization, low-precision training, pruning, or architecture transformations and often rely on staged or adaptive teacher-student schedules. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and NLP tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, what and which samples are distilled, data availability, and careful engineering of interfaces between heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, modality-agnostic approach to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as the default starting point for compression, KD provides multiple complementary signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) that—when matched to student capacity and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—produce strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is not universally sufficient: practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability and provenance, domain shift, teacher errors, and robustness/fairness constraints. A pragmatic compression pipeline therefore places KD at its center but integrates pretraining, architecture adaptation, data-aware distillation schedules, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure, and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization) and with data- or curriculum-driven strategies. Across vision, language, generative models, and policy settings, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory; however, it has clear limits related to capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data availability, and optimization instability. Real-world deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable engineering toolkit rather than a single recipe, combining careful choice of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modular approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Empirical practice shows KD yields substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy with modest accuracy loss when distillation signals, data strategies, and student architectures are aligned to deployment constraints. KD is most effective when treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that combines distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; its recurring failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, domain shift, and degraded long-tail behavior. Addressing those limits requires careful selection of distillation targets, data or synthesis strategies, multi-teacher or staged schedules, and evaluation of robustness and fairness in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. Beyond parameter reduction, KD provides learned regularization, enables transferring intermediate representations and relational structure, supports data-limited or data-free regimes, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success requires choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, augmentation, and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include distributional mismatch, capacity and representation gaps, and preserving robustness and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central but Insufficient — A Practical, Integrated Workflow for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD operates through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure), and is most valuable when composed with complementary compression primitives and data strategies. However, KD’s success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, and the provenance and coverage of distillation data; left as a standalone recipe it risks propagating teacher errors, failing on rare behaviors, and degrading under distribution shift. A pragmatic, system-level KD workflow—pretraining or designing student-friendly architectures, selecting targeted distillation signals, synthesizing or curating distillation data where needed, and pairing KD with pruning/quantization and thorough robustness evaluations—yields the most reliable path to deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression: when applied as an integrated, task-aware system it enables compact students that preserve much of a teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware surgery), careful data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols), and explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment and robustness evaluation. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits are conditional on signal selection, data and initialization choices, and evaluation for fairness and domain-shift resilience. I argue for treating KD as a configurable pipeline (signals, data, architecture, optimization) and for adopting specific practices that mitigate common failure modes in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Context-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practically proven approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-targets, intermediate representation matching, attention- and layer-aware mappings, multi- and online-teacher schemes, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and few-shot variants). KD delivers strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs when paired with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, but its benefits depend on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, adaptable component of compression pipelines while recognizing its limits and prescribing evidence-based design practices for robust, task-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient, Private, and Flexible Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks — from NLP to vision, speech, generative modeling, and graphs — KD enables deployment of high-quality models on resource-constrained devices. However, achieving reliable distillation requires attention to data availability, what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, or structural relationships), teacher design (multi-teacher and adaptive teachers), and constraints like privacy and fairness. When these factors are addressed, KD yields compact models that meet production constraints without wholesale loss of utility.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. It reliably reduces parameter counts and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with task-aware design choices and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation’s success is conditional on choices about what to transfer (logits, representations, relations), how to align teacher and student architectures, access to data or synthetic surrogates, and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and fairness failure modes. Effective deployment therefore treats distillation as a toolkit—combined with pre-training, data augmentation, and other compression primitives—rather than a single one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-signal, practical toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models in deep learning and NLP. KD methods range from softened-output matching to representation-level and relational transfers, and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices. KD routinely improves efficiency–performance trade-offs but has predictable limits—capacity mismatch, data and domain mismatch, and transfer of teacher errors or biases—that require explicit mitigation and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Bennett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Over the past decade KD has become a flexible engineering toolkit that, when combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals, student capacity, and data/optimization choices to the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, design-sensitive toolkit for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact students. Over the past decade KD has diversified from simple soft-label matching into many forms that move information at the output, representation, and relational levels; it is commonly integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data‑free or privacy‑aware techniques). Practical success hinges on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data constraints, and measuring downstream robustness and fairness; key open problems include principled teacher selection, distillation under limited or private data, and preserving rare or long‑tail behaviors during compression.

papers_seen.author: Guerra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Over the past decade KD has broadened from simple logit-matching to a flexible toolkit that includes feature- and attention-level supervision, multi-teacher and online protocols, data synthesis and data-free approaches, and composition with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on careful design choices—what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to validate robustness and fairness. Persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, preserving long-tail or rare-token behaviors in language tasks, and robustness under domain shift; addressing these requires integrated, task-aware pipelines rather than a single off-the-shelf recipe.

papers_seen.author: Combs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a configurable toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD excels when combined with architecture-aware student design, complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization), and deliberate data strategies (real-data, augmentation, or synthesis). Its practical value is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain shift determine when KD will produce reliable, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Workflows, and Limitations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, speech, and natural language tasks. KD unifies a variety of objectives—soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational losses, and multi-teacher or self-distillation—often combined with data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free) and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). When applied as an integrated, task-aware pipeline, KD frequently yields compact models that preserve most of a teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, benefits are conditional: student capacity, data availability or mismatch, architectural heterogeneity, and potential transfer of teacher errors or undesirable behaviors require careful signal selection, tailored data protocols, and targeted evaluation to ensure robust, fair, and reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Flexible — but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods have matured into a practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. These techniques have been applied across domains (vision, speech, NLP, healthcare), settings (offline compression, federated learning, continual adaptation), and architectures (ensembles, transformers, detectors, GANs). However, their success depends on factors such as the availability and nature of data used for distillation, domain mismatch between teacher and student, robustness and privacy requirements, and optimization dynamics. KD can unlock high-performing compact models when combined with task-aware design choices (e.g., feature imitation, augmentations, architecture search, or ensemble teachers), but practitioners must account for trade-offs and failure modes to use it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible suite of techniques for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression workflow but adapted to task, architecture, and data constraints, KD routinely yields substantial improvements in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Its utility spans logits-based supervision, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free pipelines. KD is not a turnkey solution: reliable deployment requires complementary methods (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful handling of teacher imperfections and limited or private data, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness.
